commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Accelerate candidate prefill and decode with CuTe
commits.pr_body:
Co-authored-by: yeshihai <71063616+yeshihai@users.noreply.github.com>

## Overview
>Thanks to @yeshihai for identifying this optimization opportunity and implementing candidate-decode scoring in Triton in #62463. This PR builds on his work with a CuTe DSL/TMA implementation and extends candidate scoring to long-context prefill. 

Add a model-local CuTe DSL scorer for DeepSeek V4.1 candidate indexers on SM90. It reads candidate keys directly from the paged FP8 cache, supports decode and eligible long-context prefill, and is enabled automatically for supported configurations.

Related to [#61830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61830). This takes a different implementation approach from [#62000](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62000), which gathers candidate keys before scoring, and [#62463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62463), which implements Triton decode scoring: this PR uses TMA/WGMMA and shares the scoring path between prefill and decode.

## Claims

- Score the existing candidate pool directly, preserving the model’s candidate-selection policy.
- Share candidate preparation across consumer layers and bound logits scratch memory by `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`.
- Enable the path through the existing `indexer_sparse_logits` configuration. Supported configurations use it by default; explicit `False` disables it.
- On the tested 512K–approximately 1M workloads, improve end-to-end output throughput by **3.2%**, reduce mean TPOT by **4.6–5.0%**, and reduce ITL P50 by **18.5–28.4%**.

## Validation



**Environment:** 8× NVIDIA H20-3e, TP8 with expert parallelism, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash , PyTorch `2.14.0+cu132`, Triton `3.8.0`, and CuTe DSL `4.8.0`.

Each workload uses eight requests at concurrency eight, **8,192 actual output tokens per request**, and three repetitions. Input lengths are 524,288 and 1,040,384 tokens; the latter leaves room for generation within the 1,048,576-token limit.

Values below are **baseline → candidate**. Throughput is the median across three runs; TPOT and ITL statistics pool samples across those runs.

| Metric | 524,288 input tokens | 1,040,384 input tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| Output throughput, tokens/s | 204.47 → 211.01 **(+3.20%)** | 84.70 → 87.43 **(+3.22%)** |
| Mean TPOT, ms/token | 19.23 → 18.28 (−4.97%) | 43.67 → 41.65 (−4.63%) |
| TPOT P50, ms/token | 19.25 → 18.28 (−5.03%) | 43.80 → 41.75 (−4.69%) |
| TPOT P95, ms/token | 34.16 → 33.05 (−3.23%) | 81.77 → 79.21 (−3.13%) |
| TPOT P99, ms/token | 34.16 → 33.07 (−3.20%) | 81.80 → 79.23 (−3.14%) |
| Mean ITL, ms | 115.57 → 109.96 (−4.85%) | 263.27 → 251.46 (−4.49%) |
| ITL P50, ms | 27.28 → 22.24 **(−18.49%)** | 35.40 → 25.34 **(−28.40%)** |
| ITL P95, ms | 1,055.38 → 1,042.63 (−1.21%) | 1,690.23 → 1,651.74 (−2.28%) |
| ITL P99, ms | 1,306.91 → 1,282.71 (−1.85%) | 2,015.30 → 1,974.49 (−2.03%) |

Throughput ranges across repetitions were 204.43–204.47 → 210.79–211.10 tokens/s at 512K, and 84.67–84.71 → 87.42–87.45 tokens/s near 1M.

**Metric interpretation:** ITL measures intervals between streamed SSE chunks. DSpark can emit multiple tokens per chunk. TPOT uses `(request latency − TTFT) / (output tokens − 1)`. These measurements cover fixed document/list-continuation bursts with overlapping prefill and decode and speculative acceptance near six tokens per step.

**Correctness and regression checks:**

- All **96 measured requests** completed with the requested output length; all **48 paired generated texts** matched.
- GSM8K, 128 questions, five-shot: **126/128 → 127/128**, with zero invalid responses. This subset is a regression check, not evidence of improved accuracy.
- Indexer regression suites: **74 passed, 23 skipped**.
- Configuration checks: **9 passed**, covering automatic selection, explicit overrides, and unsupported configurations.
- Real-weight generation comparison passed with TP4+EP, short and long prompts, DSpark CUDA graphs, logprob comparison, and nonzero speculative acceptance.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Buildkite coverage and configuration documentation are included.

<details>
<summary>Serving and benchmark reproduction</summary>

Run the same server command from each isolated checkout:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --revision 314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8566 \
  --served-model-name dsv41-bench \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"marlin","enable_jit_warmup":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32]}' \
  --generation-config vllm --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

For each input length, use its prepared custom JSONL dataset and run three repetitions. The first run’s readiness check performs one full-length request; subsequent runs use `--ready-check-timeout-sec 0`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8566 --backend openai \
  --model dsv41-bench \
  --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path "$BENCH_DATASET" \
  --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle \
  --custom-output-len 8192 \
  --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 8 --request-rate inf \
  --num-warmups 0 --ready-check-timeout-sec 1200 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 2026 \
  --save-result --save-detailed \
  --result-dir "$BENCH_RESULT_DIR" \
  --result-filename "$BENCH_RESULT_FILE" \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,95,99 --disable-tqdm
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Test and evaluation commands</summary>

```bash
# 74 passed, 23 skipped.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py

# Includes the real-weight generation comparison.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_candidate_indexer.py

# Final configuration rerun: 9 passed.
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_candidate_indexer.py \
  -k default_respects --tb=short
```

The real-weight test passed in the combined invocation. That invocation also exposed a microbatching configuration-fixture failure, which was corrected before the successful nine-case configuration rerun.

Run the evaluation against each server:

```bash
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --port 8566 --model dsv41-bench \
  --num-questions 128 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 512 \
  --max-concurrency 8 --temperature 0 --seed 42 \
  --use-chat-completions \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
```

</details>

## Details

- **Shared execution:** Prefill and decode use one candidate-scoring path. Candidate row bounds and physical-page mappings are prepared once per step and reused by consumer layers. Scoring reads paged FP8 keys directly with TMA/WGMMA and produces FP32 logits.
- **Prefill selection:** Candidate scoring is selected when the longest compressed prefill context is at least twice both the candidate-pool capacity and the largest compressed query chunk. For V4.1-Flash with query chunks up to 16K, this gives a 32K compressed-context threshold. Other prefill batches use dense scoring for the whole batch, preserving reuse of keys across queries.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Don't crash beam search on an extreme length_penalty
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

A beam search request with a large `length_penalty` returns a 500 error. `get_beam_search_score` divides by `max(seq_len, 1) ** length_penalty`:

- A large negative penalty underflows that to `0.0`, which raises `ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero`.
- A large positive one raises `OverflowError`.

Both happen while sorting beams, after generation has already run. The schemathesis test on main (`test_openapi_stateless[POST /v1/chat/completions]`, build 91958) found it:

```
vllm/entrypoints/generate/beam_search/online.py:196 beam_search
  -> utils.py:159 sort_beams_key -> utils.py:154 get_beam_search_score
ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
```

The `max(seq_len, 1)` guard from #56249 covers a zero length but not an extreme exponent.

## Change

- `get_beam_search_score` saturates instead of raising. An overflowed denominator gives a score of about 0. An underflowed one gives `-inf`, or `0.0` when the log-prob is 0. Beam order still follows the score everywhere it's finite.
- `BeamSearchParams` rejects a non-finite `length_penalty` (`inf`/`nan`) with a `VLLMValidationError`, next to the existing `beam_width` check, so the API returns 400.

This isn't a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `length_penalty`, `get_beam_search_score` and beam-search ZeroDivisionError, and found nothing related.

## Test Plan

Run on h200-0 in the CI image for main `deb148e7`, with the changed files mounted:

- `pytest tests/test_request_input_bounds.py`: 43 passed. The 4 new cases fail without the change.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files (ruff, mypy-3.10): passed.

## AI assistance

Claude Code wrote this change and the tests, from the CI failure log, and ran the checks above. @khluu has not reviewed it yet; per AGENTS.md, he needs to review every line before it merges.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Mirror release and nightly images to the vllm/vllm, vllm/vllm-rocm and vllm/vllm-xpu DockerHub aliases
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Publish release and nightly images under the short `vllm/vllm` name, and release ROCm/XPU images under `vllm/vllm-rocm` and `vllm/vllm-xpu`, alongside the existing `vllm/vllm-openai*` repos. Each alias has the same digest as its source tag.

## Claims

- **Release** (`publish-release-images.sh`):

  | Source | Also published as |
  |---|---|
  | `vllm/vllm-openai:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai:{latest,vX}-efa` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-efa` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-rocm` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:{latest,vX}-<variant>` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-<variant>` (e.g. `-rocm100`) |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-cpu` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-xpu` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:*` (all release tags, incl. `-base`) | `vllm/vllm-rocm:*` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:*` (all release tags, incl. `-x86_64`) | `vllm/vllm-xpu:*` |

- **Nightly** (`push-nightly-builds{,-cpu}.sh`, `xpu/push-nightly-builds-xpu.sh`, `rocm/publish.sh`): the mutable tag is also published as `vllm/vllm:nightly`, `nightly-cu134`, `nightly-cpu`, `nightly-xpu`, `nightly-rocm` and `nightly-<variant>` (e.g. `nightly-rocm100`).
- **Docs:** `docs/deployment/docker.md` gets a "Short image names" section with this mapping.

## Validation

- v0.33.0 was aliased by hand with this mapping (`crane copy`). Every alias digest matches its source, e.g. `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0` = `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0` = `sha256:d825baf9ce4b…`, `vllm/vllm-rocm:v0.33.0` = `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.33.0` = `sha256:4fcd39b758b6…` (16/16 `vllm/vllm-rocm` + `vllm/vllm-xpu` tags match).
- Digest behaviour of `docker buildx imagetools create`, tested against a local `registry:2`:

  | Source | Copy keeps the digest? |
  |---|---|
  | OCI index / Docker `manifest.list.v2` (1 or 2 entries, as `docker manifest create` makes) | yes |
  | Single-arch manifest (by tag or by digest) | **no**: wrapped in a new 1-entry list |
  | One `create` call with `-t` in several repos | yes: all tags get one digest |

- Dry run of every target (`publish-release-images.sh rocm|xpu`, the four nightly scripts, `rocm/publish.sh rocm images` with `NIGHTLY=1`, `NIGHTLY=0` and `ALIAS_HUB=`) with `docker`/`aws`/`buildkite-agent` stubbed: prints exactly the tags above, and nothing under `vllm/vllm` for `NIGHTLY=0` or `ALIAS_HUB=`.
- `bash -n`, shellcheck and pre-commit pass (no new shellcheck findings).
- Not exercised in CI: these scripts only run in the release pipeline. The first nightly after merge and the v0.34.0 release are the first real runs. `vllmbot` can already push to `vllm/vllm-rocm` and `vllm/vllm-xpu` (used for the v0.33.0 copies).

## Details

- **ROCm images are single-arch**, so copying a published ROCm tag with `imagetools create` would wrap it and change its digest. The ROCm aliases (`vllm/vllm:*-rocm*`, `vllm/vllm-rocm:*`) are therefore extra `-t` flags on the `create` call that writes the canonical tags. CUDA, EFA, CPU and XPU copy a manifest list, which keeps the digest. XPU pushes the same image and list to both repos in a loop.
- **Nightly aliases are mutable tags only.** Every `vllm/vllm` nightly family shares the `nightly-` prefix, so `cleanup-nightly-builds.sh` could not prune commit tags per family, and it would delete the mutable `nightly-<suffix>` tags as well. Commit-pinned, per-arch and `base-nightly` tags stay in the canonical repos, so `vllm/vllm` needs no cleanup.
- `rocm/publish.sh` takes `ALIAS_HUB` (default `vllm/vllm`, empty to skip), like the existing `HUB` override.
- Not covered: `-rocm72` release tags (not published by this script), the EFA nightly (pending in #64028), and nightlies in `vllm/vllm-rocm` / `vllm/vllm-xpu`.
- Not a duplicate: no other open PR touches these scripts for aliasing (`gh pr list --search "publish-release-images in:files"`; #64028 only adds the EFA nightly).

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Fuse GELU + NVFP4 quant for BERT-style FFNs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

NVFP4 BERT, RoBERTa and XLM-R write the FFN's GELU output in 16 bits and read it back to quantize it for the down projection. This PR fuses GELU into that quant by generalizing the Triton ReLU2 + NVFP4 producer (#59384) into `act_nvfp4_quant.py`, and routes BERT's FFN through the manual act+quant fusion (`maybe_fused_act_quant`, #51415). The up projection keeps its bias, which SM120's CUTLASS NVFP4 GEMM adds in its epilogue (#61821).

## Claims

- `act_nvfp4_quant.py`: the Triton producer gains an exact (erf) GELU variant for fp16 and bf16 input, registered on SM12x. The block max now takes |x|, since GELU can be negative; ReLU2's output never is, so its results are unchanged.
- BERT's FFN fuses GELU + NVFP4 quant only when the down projection takes NVFP4 input, so FP16 and FP8 are unchanged.
- `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` NVFP4 on an RTX PRO 6000 with `--linear-backend cutlass`: 18-21% less GPU time, with scores bitwise identical to main. On the default FlashInfer CUTLASS backend, which adds the bias in a separate kernel, about 1% less.

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), torch 2.14.0, FlashInfer 0.7.3, main fa211f2d + #65149.

- `pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py`: 181 passed, 38 skipped (the ReLU2 NVFP4 tests are SM10x-only). The new GELU test matches `torch.compile`d GELU + `scaled_fp4_quant` bitwise, all-negative rows included.

GPU kernel time of one `classify` call on 128 sequences (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, `LLM(runner="pooling", dtype="float16")`, mean of 3 runs, spread <= 0.13 ms):

| Tokens/seq | `cutlass`: main | `cutlass`: this PR | default: main | default: this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 160 | 26.30 ms | 20.68 ms (-21.4%) | 27.73 ms | 27.36 ms (-1.3%) |
| 320 | 52.45 ms | 41.44 ms (-21.0%) | 60.21 ms | 59.46 ms (-1.2%) |
| 640 | 119.01 ms | 97.29 ms (-18.3%) | 134.63 ms | 133.19 ms (-1.1%) |

Recall@10 vs PyTorch FP32 on all 741 questions (Ko-StrategyQA / MIRACL-ko): with `cutlass`, the scores are identical to main (0.874 / 0.929); with the default backend, 0.879 / 0.929 on main (fa211f2d alone) and 0.874 / 0.937 with this PR, where main's Inductor fuses the bias add into GELU without rounding the sum to fp16.

GELU + NVFP4 quant alone (K = 4096, fp16, CUDA graph replay), against the C++ variant of the SiLU-and-mul kernel that an earlier revision of this PR used:

| M | 1 | 128 | 1024 | 4096 | 20480 | 81920 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main: GELU + `scaled_fp4_quant` | 1.98 us | 2.62 us | 7.35 us | 24.40 us | 349.3 us | 1490.2 us |
| this PR: Triton | 1.76 us | 2.19 us | 6.47 us | 20.07 us | 146.4 us | 576.2 us |
| earlier revision: C++ | 1.36 us | 1.56 us | 6.05 us | 13.23 us | 146.4 us | 580.7 us |

## Details

- **Bias:** FlashInfer's `mm_fp4` takes no bias, so its backends add it in a separate kernel and gain little here. A bias in those GEMMs would extend the gain to them without changing this PR.
- **SM12x only:** the GELU variant is registered where I validated it; ReLU2 stays on SM10x.
- **Duplicates:** no open PR fuses exact GELU into NVFP4 quant.
- **CI:** `tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py` runs in `(B200) Miscellaneous Kernels`, which covers the ReLU2 path after the rename and the |x| change; the GELU test needs SM12x and skips there. Validated at TP=1 only.
- **AI assistance:** prepared with Claude Code (kernel, wiring, tests, validation, this text). I reviewed every changed line and the results.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Pass NewRequestData to speculator add_request; add shutdown hook
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Extend the `BaseSpeculator` request hooks from vllm-project/vllm#60339 so that custom speculators (vllm-project/vllm#63205) that keep per-request state outside vLLM can track their requests.

## Claims

- `add_request(req_index, new_req_data)` also receives the request's `NewRequestData`, as `model_state.add_request` does.
- New `shutdown()`, called when the model runner shuts down. By default it releases the speculator's draft model, which the runner used to do.
- Both stay no-ops by default, so in-tree speculators behave as before.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`: the new `test_speculator_request_hooks` passes. It fails if the runner doesn't pass `new_req_data` to `add_request`, calls `on_requests_finished` after freeing the slot, or reports a preempted request to it.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_speculator.py` needs CUDA, so it wasn't run locally; CI's V1 Spec Decode step runs it.
- End to end on one B300 (n-gram drafting, a KV cache small enough to force a preemption, one request aborted mid-decode), with the hooks overridden to record calls. Every request got `add_request`, then `on_requests_finished` before its slot was freed. The preempted request got no hook when its slot was freed, and `add_request` again when it resumed. `shutdown` ran once. With sync scheduling, greedy outputs and spec decode counters match the unpatched build.

## Details

- Use case: a speculator that drafts on a remote service. A custom scheduler opens and releases each request's remote session and puts the session ID in `SamplingParams.extra_args`. The speculator reads the ID in `add_request` to bind that slot's connection, and closes its connections in `shutdown`.
- `shutdown` also covers requests still in the runner when it shuts down. The runner learns that a request finished at the next step, so a request that finishes in the last step never reaches `on_requests_finished`.
- Breaking change: `add_request` gains a parameter. It was added by vllm-project/vllm#60339, and its only in-tree override, the suffix speculator, is updated here.
- The hooks run on the host, and add no GPU synchronization.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Keep HIP uninitialized in the GPU memory wait
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the test memory wait initializes HIP in the test process, so vLLM spawns instead of forks every EngineCore and worker created after it. This polls from a forked child while HIP is still uninitialized, so engines fork as they do on CUDA. Found while making the AMD PP equivalence nightly from #67354 fit in its timeout ([build 102669](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102669#01a1d8d6-1994-4a2b-8a42-5859eb7d9f02) timed out at 3 h).

## Claims

- `VllmRunner` tests on ROCm no longer force `spawn` for EngineCore and workers ("We must use the `spawn` ... Reasons: CUDA is initialized")
- About 62 s saved per PP=4 `test_pp_equivalence` case on MI300X, the cold vLLM import of each spawned engine process
- The memory query itself is unchanged, so the HIP logical-device semantics from #57450 stay; CUDA and XPU are untouched

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), local, idle node, GPUs 0-3, same tree in both arms except `tests/utils.py`. 8 architectures of `models/test_pp_equivalence.py -m 'distributed(num_gpus=4)'`, 3 alternating runs per arm, per-test time from JUnit XML.

| Arch | Before (median s) | After (median s) |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma3 | 163 | 99 |
| GptOss | 140 | 75 |
| Llama | 132 | 69 |
| Mixtral | 125 | 65 |
| Qwen3 | 128 | 66 |
| Qwen3Next | 130 | 68 |
| Kolibri1 | 144 | 144 |
| Ministral3 | 133 | 136 |
| **Suite (8 passed, 1 skipped)** | 18:16 – 18:32, 8 spawns | 12:05 – 12:30, 2 spawns |

```bash
cd tests
VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1 pytest -v -s models/test_pp_equivalence.py -m 'distributed(num_gpus=4)' \
  -k "LlamaForCausalLM or Qwen3ForCausalLM or GptOssForCausalLM or Gemma3ForCausalLM or MixtralForCausalLM or Qwen3NextForCausalLM or Ministral3ForCausalLM or Kolibri1ForCausalLM"
```

With the change, these pass: the full PP=4 suite with #67354 (74 passed, 2 xfailed, 11 skipped), its PP=2 subset 10/10, `basic_correctness -m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)' -k 'not ray'`, `v1/shutdown`, `distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py`, `v1/metrics/test_engine_logger_apis.py`, a `models/test_initialization.py` subset, `models/language -m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)'` and `models/language/pooling/test_embedding.py`. A direct check shows the caller stays HIP-free, `get_mp_context()` returns `fork`, and a timeout still raises `ValueError` in the caller.

## Details

#57450 switched the ROCm query in `record_gpu_memory_usage_stats` to `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info` for correct numbers on MI355 partitions, which initializes HIP in the caller. `VllmRunner.__init__` calls `wait_for_memory_to_settle` before `LLM()`, so `_maybe_force_spawn` sees "CUDA is initialized" and switches the rest of the test process to `spawn`. When HIP is not yet initialized, `wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear` now runs in a one-worker fork `ProcessPoolExecutor`. The child calls `torch.cuda.init()`, which keeps it on the in-process path instead of forking again, and runs the unchanged loop. Callers that already initialized HIP keep the in-process path.

Behavior change: most ROCm `VllmRunner` tests now fork EngineCore and workers, like CUDA. A test still spawns if something initialized HIP in its process first (an `HfRunner`, an in-process GPU tensor), so the start method can depend on earlier tests in the same process. Groups that need `spawn` already export `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` and are unaffected. Forking also brings Python's "process is multi-threaded, use of fork()" DeprecationWarning, as on CUDA.

Known limits:
- Kolibri1 and Ministral3 still spawn. Their quantization lookup imports `vllm/models/deepseek_v41`, and `model_executor/layers/mhc.py` evaluates its AITER capability flags at import time, which initializes HIP. That needs its own fix.
- The Ray cases of `test_models_distributed` fail on this node with and without this change, because two Ray workers keep their GPU memory after EngineCore shutdown.
- #66670 changes the same function. If it lands after this, its new `idle_bytes` argument has to be added to the `pool.submit` call here.

No open PR addresses the spawn (searched `wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear`, `record_gpu_memory_usage_stats`, ROCm memory wait fork).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Quant] LUT-B: fit per-channel block32 weight scales
commits.pr_body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"mgoin"} -->
_Requested by **Misha** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018k9kprp2xqm4XNPQE9WVgy?thread=cmsg_018k9kprp2xqm4XNPQE9WVgy2eNR5HZxadCu8K7fVouu5z)_

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Online LUT-B (`--quantization lut_b_moe`, #62759) now fits weight scales at the granularity the Rubin instruction actually takes: one UE8M0 per output channel per 32 K (`[N, K/32]`). Before, it fit one exponent per 8x64 codebook tile and repeat-interleaved it into that layout. This lines vLLM up with a block32-scale LUT-B checkpoint format (see vllm-project/compressed-tensors#996 discussion).

## Claims

- `quantize_lut_b` returns scales as `[E, N, K/32]`. `lut_b_to_sm107_tiles` consumes them directly with no repeat-interleave, and `dequantize_lut_b` (emulation) applies them per block.
- Reconstruction error is never worse than one scale per tile, and it is 1.09x to 1.73x lower on the synthetic weights below.
- The SM107 runtime image (7168 B per 128x128 tile) and the kernel are unchanged, so there is no runtime memory or speed change. The B-scale bytes were already stored and loaded at full granularity.

## Validation

CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest --noconftest tests/kernels/moe/test_lut_b_moe.py`: 6 passed, 10 skipped (the GPU emulation and SM107 tests need a GPU). Passed: `test_pack_roundtrip`, `test_quantize_format_and_fit`, `test_quantize_block_scales_follow_rows` (new), `test_quantize_scale_refinement_never_hurts` (new), `test_quantize_preserves_zeros`, `test_sm107_tile_layout` (the bit-exact layout decoder, now with distinct scales per row).

Relative squared reconstruction error, `[512, 1024]` weights x 0.02, old (`main`) vs this PR, CPU:

| weights | main (one scale per tile) | better of tied / amax | + exponent search (this PR) | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gaussian | 0.0371 | 0.0358 | 0.0340 | 1.09x |
| Student-t (3 dof) | 0.0610 | 0.0475 | 0.0426 | 1.43x |
| Gaussian x lognormal row scale | 0.0546 | 0.0348 | 0.0316 | 1.73x |
| Gaussian x lognormal row and column scale | 0.0629 | 0.0461 | 0.0409 | 1.54x |

Quantization time for one 512x1024 weight on CPU: 0.04 s on main, 0.08 s with this PR.

**Rubin (Vera Rubin, 1 GPU, built from source at 4000bde):**
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_lut_b_moe.py`, `tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py`, `tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_lut_b_moe`: 62 passed, 0 skipped. This includes `test_sm107_gemm_exact` (bit-exact against an independent decoder) and all `test_sm107_matches_emulation` cases.
- GSM8K, `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash`, full 1319 questions, 5-shot chat, thinking off, max 2048 generated tokens, `--quantization lut_b_moe` on the native SM107 path (`tcgen05.mma.kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale.decompress::lut::b.block32`, MXFP8 activations):

| quantizer (same build and node) | strict | flexible | online quantization |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, one scale per tile | 0.832 | 0.832 | 96 s |
| this PR, block32 + exponent search | **0.853** | **0.852** | 238 s |

BF16 scores 0.857 with the same eval settings (earlier run). The stderr is about 0.010, so +0.021 is about 2 stderr.

## Details

- The hardware takes the codebook (`[book]`, 8 channels x K64) and the B scale (`[sfb]`, block32) as separate TMEM operands of `tcgen05.mma.kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale.decompress::lut::b.block32`, so the 16 scales of a tile can differ.
- Each tile is first fitted twice:
  - with all 16 exponents tied to the tile maximum, which matches today's result exactly;
  - with each block's exponent taken from its own amax. Here the codebook is fitted by weighted Lloyd, with each value weighted by its scale squared, so the loss is the error of the rescaled weights.
- The fit with the lower loss is kept.
- Picking exponents from block amaxes alone is worse than one tile scale on i.i.d. Gaussian weights (0.0381 vs 0.0371). Blocks that differ only by amax noise land on different power-of-two steps, and the shared 8-entry codebook then has to cover both copies.
- So `num_scale_rounds` (default 4) rounds of coordinate descent follow:
  - move each block's exponent by -1, 0 or +1, whichever decodes that block best with the current codebook (the -1 move lets a block clip its largest values in exchange for finer steps elsewhere);
  - refit the codebook with 4 warm-started weighted Lloyd iterations.
- Every step is kept only where it lowers the error, so the result is never worse than one scale per tile. `num_scale_rounds=0` reproduces the two-fit result bit for bit.
- Tradeoff: online quantization at load time is about 2.5x slower on GLM-4.7-Flash (238 s vs 96 s; the baseline run shared the node with a build, so its time is approximate). `num_scale_rounds` can be lowered if that matters.
- Logical format size goes from 3.14 to 3.375 bits per weight. The GPU-resident SM107 image is 3.5 bpw either way.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Import the SM80/SM90 metadata builders lazily
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since #66497, `(CPU) V1 Others` fails on main. `test_deepseek_v41_metadata_graphs_match_the_forward_graphs` (4 cases) imports the DeepSeek-V4.1 metadata-graph runtime, which now imports the SM80/SM90 builders at module load, and their modules need `cuda.bindings` and `cutlass`, which the CPU image doesn't have. This PR imports those builders the first time the recordable set is used, so the runtime imports without them.

Failing main builds: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103197, https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103198, https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103199. The last main run of the step before #66497 passed: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103179.

## Claims

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/runtime/metadata_graphs.py` imports on a machine without `cuda.bindings` or `cutlass`, and `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py` passes in the CPU test image again.
- Which builders the recording accepts is unchanged: the same 10 classes, now returned by a cached `_recordable_builders()` instead of the module constant `_RECORDABLE_BUILDERS`.
- No change on GPU: `can_record` is the only caller, and it runs outside CUDA graph capture.

## Validation

In the CPU test image built for this PR's base (`vllm-ci-test-repo:<sha>-arm64-cpu`, which has neither `cuda.bindings` nor `cutlass`), from `/vllm-workspace/tests`:

```
pytest -q v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py
```

- As on main: `4 failed, 36 passed`, each failure `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cuda'` raised from `ampere/mqa_logits.py:61`, reached through `runtime/metadata_graphs.py:46`.
- With this PR's `metadata_graphs.py` copied over the installed module: `40 passed`.
- CI on this PR's head (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103226): `(CPU) V1 Others` ran and passed, the 4 cases `PASSED`, `40 passed` for the file, no retries.
- `pre-commit` on both files: clean.
- Not run: `test_metadata_graph_state.py`, which only changes from the constant to the function. It needs the SM80/SM90 kernel packages and runs in the nightly `(8xH100) DeepSeek-V4.1 SM80 and SM90 Decode` step, which a PR build doesn't run.

## Details

- **Root cause:** #66497 added `from ..ampere...` and `from ..hopper...` imports at the top of `runtime/metadata_graphs.py` to list those builders as recordable. `ampere/attention.py` imports `ampere/indexer.py`, which imports `ampere/mqa_logits.py`, whose first lines are `import cuda.bindings.driver` and `import cutlass`. Before #66497 the runtime imported neither package.
- **Why not make `mqa_logits.py` import lazily:** its kernels are `@cute.jit` functions defined at module level, and about a dozen other `ampere/` modules import `cutlass` at the top too. The runtime is the one place that pulls them in for a test that only needs capture keys.
- **Why not skip the test without `cuda.bindings`:** `test_cudagraph_manager.py` runs only in `(CPU) V1 Others`, so a skip would leave these 4 cases running nowhere.
- `can_record` is called when recording starts, before the capture loop, and during a step only with `not for_capture`; its result is cached per instance. On SM80/SM90 the builder modules are already imported by the model's attention layers.
- **Why #66497's PR build didn't catch it:** the test selector matched the file to `(CPU) V1 Others` and then dropped the step on its coverage record (`dropped-by-coverage`, reproduced locally with `ci-select` and the same record). #66497 also changed a log message inside `replay()`, so the file's changed names weren't all import-time, and the selector required the step to have called a changed function; V1 Others calls `capture_keys`, not `replay`. Run locally on this PR's diff, the selector keeps the step, so this PR's build runs the test.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Use value-only reduction for FP8 group quantization
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #25094 

Slack context: https://vllm-dev.slack.com/archives/C08K1FAHFPH/p1790784879162549

## Summary

 - The issue is simply that the compiled one uses `torch.max(...)[0]` which causes a reduction over values and indices, whereas the cuda one correctly only reduces values.
 - Replacing it with `amax()` immediately resolves the issue and compiled is now uniformly faster than cuda.
 - As per slack discussion, in the bench repro below we compile it with the maximum value of `num_tokens`.
 - The bench also checked that the change preserves the output of the previous implementation exactly.

## Environment

H200 sm90, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, driver 580.126.09, vLLM 2fc3f9

## Numbers

| compile max | tokens | hidden | before (us) | after (us) | CUDA (us) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 | 512 | 2048 | 2.766 | 2.497 | 2.603 |
| 8192 | 8192 | 2048 | 24.500 | 17.734 | 22.854 |
| 8192 | 512 | 4096 | 4.436 | 3.541 | 3.971 |
| 8192 | 8192 | 4096 | 48.129 | 34.885 | 43.664 |
| 8192 | 512 | 7168 | 6.513 | 4.918 | 5.871 |
| 8192 | 8192 | 7168 | 82.865 | 59.053 | 74.613 |
| 16384 | 512 | 2048 | 2.954 | 2.514 | 2.601 |
| 16384 | 16384 | 2048 | 48.107 | 34.819 | 43.671 |
| 16384 | 512 | 4096 | 4.480 | 3.540 | 3.973 |
| 16384 | 16384 | 4096 | 94.161 | 66.879 | 85.002 |
| 16384 | 512 | 7168 | 6.416 | 4.903 | 5.890 |
| 16384 | 16384 | 7168 | 162.552 | 115.090 | 146.931 |

Before: ~10% slower than cuda. After: upto 20% faster than cuda.

## Long

Initially, the issue seemed to be an autotuning quirk, where inductor was choosing block size `XBLOCK=32` even though it was slower than `XBLOCK=8`, but this is an issue only for small values of `num_tokens` like 1024. Higher than that (relevant values are 8192 and 16384), it did use `XBLOCK=8` and the issue turned out to be an unnecessary reduction over indices in the generated kernel itself, as described below:

For `max()[0]`, Inductor generated:

```py
  tmp5 = tl.broadcast_to(rindex, tmp4.shape)
  tmp3_val, tmp3_idx = triton_helpers.max_with_index(tmp4, tmp5, 1)
  tmp3 = tmp3_val[:, None]
```

The fix, using `amax()`, makes it generate:

```py
  tmp5 = triton_helpers.max2(tmp4, 1)[:, None].to(tl.float32)
```

|  | max()[0] | amax() |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Static instructions | 480 | 360 |
| SHFL.BFLY | 6 | 3 |
| Integer SEL | 33 | 17 |
| Registers | 29 | 30 |


The slowdown is not register pressure related, and seems to be cos of the extra instructions.

## Reproducer

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```py
import torch

from vllm.benchmarks.lib.utils import default_vllm_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.input_quant_fp8 import (
    QuantFP8,
    _FP8_DTYPE,
    _FP8_MAX,
    _FP8_MIN,
    _FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR,
)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import GroupShape
from vllm.triton_utils import triton


torch._dynamo.config.automatic_dynamic_shapes = False


def quantize(x: torch.Tensor, value_only: bool):
    shape = x.shape
    grouped = x.view(-1, x.shape[-1] // 128, 128)
    if value_only:
        absmax = grouped.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True).float()
    else:
        absmax = grouped.abs().max(dim=-1, keepdim=True)[0].float()
    scales = torch.exp2(torch.ceil(torch.log2(absmax / _FP8_MAX)))
    scales = scales.clamp(min=_FP8_MIN_SCALING_FACTOR)
    output = (grouped / scales).clamp(_FP8_MIN, _FP8_MAX).to(_FP8_DTYPE)
    return output.view(shape), scales.squeeze(-1)


def before(x):
    return quantize(x, False)


def after(x):
    return quantize(x, True)


def run(compile_max: int):
    for hidden in (2048, 4096, 7168):
        quant = QuantFP8(False, GroupShape(1, 128), column_major_scales=False)
        assert quant.use_ue8m0

        before_compiled = torch.compile(before, fullgraph=True, dynamic=False)
        after_compiled = torch.compile(after, fullgraph=True, dynamic=False)

        compile_input = torch.randn(
            compile_max, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
        )
        torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(compile_input, 0)
        before_compiled(compile_input)
        after_compiled(compile_input)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

        for tokens in (512, compile_max):
            x = torch.randn(tokens, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
            old = before_compiled(x)
            new = after_compiled(x)
            torch.testing.assert_close(new[0].float(), old[0].float(), rtol=0, atol=0)
            torch.testing.assert_close(new[1], old[1], rtol=0, atol=0)

            bench = lambda fn: 1000 * triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(fn)
            old_us = bench(lambda: before_compiled(x))
            new_us = bench(lambda: after_compiled(x))
            cuda_us = bench(lambda: quant.forward_cuda(x))
            print(
                f"| {compile_max} | {tokens} | {hidden} | "
                f"{old_us:.3f} | {new_us:.3f} | {cuda_us:.3f} |"
            )


@default_vllm_config()
def main():
    from torch._inductor.utils import fresh_inductor_cache

    print("| compile max | tokens | hidden | before (us) | after (us) | CUDA (us) |")
    print("|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|")

    for compile_max in (8192, 16384):
        with fresh_inductor_cache():
            torch._dynamo.reset()
            run(compile_max)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kernel] Extend skinny gemm N=5 to N=8 cases on GFX12 (RDNA4) using  SWMMAC optimization
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR adds an optimized ROCm GFX12 (RDNA4) SWMMAC-based skinny GEMM path.

The new path targets serving workloads with low max concurrency, matching the benchmarked decode GEMM range of N=5-8. The implementation uses sparse wave matrix multiply-accumulate instructions on GFX12 (RDNA4) to improve throughput for these skinny GEMM cases, while keeping the existing fallback path for unsupported cases.

Skinny GEMMs can be important for ROCm/GFX12 (RDNA4) serving performance, which is often used in local or small-scale serving setups. In these deployments, the server is expected to handle single users, or a small number of users with a relatively lower request rate, so the active decode batch can remain small instead of being filled to a large batch size.

This optimization follows the same general direction described in the Hugging Face technical blog, [*Creating custom kernels for the AMD MI300*](https://huggingface.co/blog/mi300kernels). The blog discusses custom kernels for AMD MI300X vLLM serving and describes a skinny GEMM optimization for inputs with 8 or fewer rows.

The key idea is to map each logical skinny A row into two adjacent SWMMAC sparse rows. The first sparse row selects one set of 16-bit pairs from `A[n, :]`, and the second sparse row selects the complementary pairs from the same logical row. Both sparse rows multiply with the same normal `B[32 x 16]` fragment, producing two partial accumulator rows. The epilogue then adds the adjacent partial rows back together to recover the final logical output row. This interleaved sparse-row layout lets the kernel use the SWMMAC instruction shape more effectively for N=5-8 instead of leaving the skinny rows underfilled.

A related optimization direction is also being explored in IREE: [*[AMDGPU][Codegen] Optimizing skinny GEMM workloads with sparse matrix instructions*](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/22863). The IREE issue describes using sparse matrix instructions to optimize skinny GEMM workloads on AMD CDNA GPUs. Although the IREE discussion focuses on IREE codegen and CDNA-style sparse MFMA examples, the motivation is closely related: skinny GEMM workloads can waste matrix instruction capacity due to padding or under-filled dimensions, and sparse matrix instructions can recover more effective throughput.

Note: this PR is not a direct port of either implementation. It adapts the same idea to the vLLM ROCm/GFX12 (RDNA4) path using SWMMAC with tuned optimization strategies for the measured small-N decode GEMM cases.

**This PR:**

* Adds a GFX12 (RDNA4) SWMMAC skinny GEMM kernel path
* Targets decode GEMM shapes with N=5-8
* Preserves the existing fallback path for unsupported cases
* Adds correctness coverage for the new SWMMAC path across:

  * N = 5, 6, 7, 8
  * FP16 and BF16, matching the existing skinny GEMM dtype coverage
  * Multiple M/K sizes
  * Aligned (divisible by 16) and non-aligned M dimensions 
  * Large-shape cases

Note: N=4 was also evaluated, but it did not show a benefit in this implementation, so this PR keeps the optimized path scoped to N=5-8.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py::test_rocm_swmmac_gemm_kernel
```

### GSM8K end-to-end accuracy

The GSM8K run was performed with the vLLM server launched using --max-num-seqs 8, and lm_eval used num_concurrent=8. This keeps the active decode batch within the targeted skinny GEMM range and exercises the SWMMAC N=5-8 paths.

**Model:** `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`

Server command:
```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
  ```

Benchmark command:
```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=${MODEL},base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=1024,max_length=8192,timeout=60000" \
  --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --output_path ./results_qwen3_4b_gsm8k \
  --log_samples
```


### Performance Benchmark

- **Hardware:** GPU: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201, GFX12 (RDNA4), **x1** | CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor, **x32**  |  RAM: 123Gi
- **Model:** Qwen/Qwen3-4B
- **Benchmark setup:**
  - **Concurrency:** 5, 6, 7, 8
  - **Input/output token shapes:** 512/128, 1024/256, 2048/128, 2048/512, 4096/512, 8192/512, 1024/2048, 512/4096, 512/8192

Baseline commit (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/6bdabbad5bce747865fd3a249658518a4269cc22):


Server script:
```bash

set -euo pipefail

rm -rf ~/.cache/vllm

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --dtype auto \

```

Benchmark script:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL=${BASE_URL:-http://localhost:8000}
RESULT_DIR=${RESULT_DIR:-./bench-results}
RESULT_PREFIX=${RESULT_PREFIX:-qwen3-4b}

  "512 128" \

  "512 4096" \

  set -- $workload

  for C in ${CONCURRENCIES}; do
    NUM_PROMPTS=$((C * 10))

    vllm bench serve \

      --request-rate inf \
      --max-concurrency "${C}" \
      --num-warmups "${NUM_WARMUPS}" \
      --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
      --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
      --save-result \
      --result-dir "${RESULT_DIR}" \
      --result-filename "${RESULT_PREFIX}-${INPUT_LEN}-${OUTPUT_LEN}-C${C}.json" \
      --metadata model=qwen3-4b concurrency="${C}" workload=random_${INPUT_LEN}_${OUTPUT_LEN} num_prompts="${NUM_PROMPTS}"
  done

```


## Test Results

### Unit tests
216 passed, 16 warnings in 52.55s

### GSM8K end-to-end accuracy

| Version | flexible-extract exact_match | strict-match exact_match | Request progress |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Baseline** | 0.8613 ± 0.0095 | 0.8650 ± 0.0094 | 1319 requests in 11:13, 1.96 it/s |
| **SWMMAC** | 0.8605 ± 0.0095 | 0.8666 ± 0.0094 | 1319 requests in 09:48, 2.24 it/s |

*The GSM8K accuracy is comparable between the baseline and SWMMAC runs. The SWMMAC run also completed faster in this setup.*

commits.pr_body:
Use all-to-all and fused Triton summation for inputs above 4 MiB, followed by all-gather for all-reduce. Keep the existing all-gather path for smaller inputs and uneven reduce-scatter during graph capture.

Keep gather and sharded all-reduce implementations separate, with explicit dispatch at the entry point. Accumulate in FP32 on both paths and cast back to the input dtype once.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Add DSpine support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Add DSpine speculative decoding for Qwen, based on [Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36173) and the [Tencent reference implementation](https://github.com/Tencent/DSpine). - Supports Tencent and Speculators checkpoint layouts through one model implementation. - Reuses existing candidate sampling and verification; DSpine supplies its candidate transition scores. - Adds a Qwen3.8-27B GSM8K regression to the existing DFlash test suite and CI configuration. The implementation extends the existing DFlash/DFlash2 paths with checkpoint-format adaptation and TP-aware transition scoring, without adding a separate sampling implementation. ## Validation Evaluated `tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16` with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` on **one H100 80GB**, BF16, TP=1, FA3, concurrency 8, and **15 draft tokens**. The five-dataset acceptance runs use **thinking enabled**, `reasoning_effort=xhigh`, a 4,096-token output cap, and no prefix caching. T0 uses greedy drafts; T1 uses probabilistic drafts with target sampling `top_p=0.95, top_k=20`. Each result below is **mean per-response acceptance length / pooled acceptance length**. | Dataset | Responses per run | T0 | T1 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GSM8K | 1,319 | 6.9271 / 5.9024 | 6.4762 / 5.4559 | | MATH-500 | 500 | 6.3780 / 5.1225 | 5.8710 / 4.6984 | | HumanEval | 164 | 5.7120 / 5.2160 | 5.1886 / 4.6133 | | MBPP | 500 | 5.9092 / 5.1499 | 5.4030 / 4.6400 | | MT-Bench | 160 | 4.6933 / 4.1340 | 4.3010 / 3.7483 | The acceptance numbers below were measured with draft revision `5f54174d301dbca65d9aa4448dc47e56732d9a12`. The server command uses the [updated Hugging Face revision](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16/tree/260a6c23070ca873ff1a5f33b7119ac3f6a245ee), which declares `DSpineDraftModel` in its config.
Start the T1 server from the vLLM checkout ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --revision 37561816e66b5b9153b1b64c10968c18c1e6f4a0 \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18481 \ --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --language-model-only \ --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --generation-config vllm --seed 0 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASH_ATTN","flash_attn_version":3}' \ --speculative-config '{ "model":"tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16", "revision":"260a6c23070ca873ff1a5f33b7119ac3f6a245ee", "method":"dflash", "num_speculative_tokens":15, "enable_adaptive_verification":false, "draft_sample_method":"probabilistic" }' \ --per-request-spec-decode-metrics summary ```
Once the server is ready, run from the Speculators checkout with its evaluation dependencies installed:
Run the T1 GSM8K acceptance evaluation ```bash python /home/shanjiaz/dspine-evaluations/tencent-b16-acceptance-aiperf-20261110/speculators-checkout/scripts/evaluate/evaluate.py \ acceptance \ --dataset gsm8k \ --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --tokenizer-revision 37561816e66b5b9153b1b64c10968c18c1e6f4a0 \ --url http://127.0.0.1:18481 \ --num-conversations 1319 \ --concurrency 8 \ --extra-inputs '{"temperature": 1, "max_completion_tokens": 4096, "reasoning_effort": "xhigh", "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20}' \ --output-artifact-dir /home/shanjiaz/dspine-evaluations/tencent-b16-probabilistic-aiperf-20261111/t1-gsm8k ```
Tested higher concurrency with adaptive verification on/off on 8 h100s: ## Note **Weight loading:** Tencent stacks independent layer matrices in shared checkpoint tensors; we unpack them into per-layer `ReplicatedLinear` modules and map names through the existing DFlash loader, preserving the learned values and using the same model implementation for both checkpoint layouts. AI assistance was used in implementation and validation. ---

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Share the narrow dummy FP8 fixture with the NVFP4 fusion test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the `:nvidia: (B200) [Nightly] Fusion E2E Config Sweep` failure tracked in #67307. `test_tp1_fp4_mixed_precision_act_fusion[...Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4...]` started failing after #67693 changed the dummy FP8 weights. This PR moves #67753's narrow dummy FP8 fixture into `tests/conftest.py` as `narrow_dummy_fp8_weights`, and uses it in both the HiSparse tests and this fusion test.

## Root cause

- The test loads the model with `load_format="dummy"`. It compares the fused (`silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`) and unfused NVFP4 MLP outputs with `assert_close(atol=1e-1, rtol=1e-1)`. The two paths are not bitwise equal: the unfused path rounds the SiLU output to bf16 before quantizing, so a few elements land one FP4 step apart.
- Since #67693, `initialize_single_dummy_weight` fills every 8-bit float param with random codes across the FP8 range. Dense NVFP4 linears (`KNvfp4Static`) store their block scales `weight_scale` as `float8_e4m3fn`, without the positive `dummy_weight_value` that the NVFP4 MoE path sets. So these scales are now signed and up to ±448, where they used to be within ±1.
- The larger activations turn that one-step rounding difference into large absolute errors. Nightly [102861](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102861): 103 / 5120 elements mismatch, greatest absolute difference 1.41. The test passed in nightly 102740, before #67693 merged.

## Changes

- `tests/conftest.py`: new `narrow_dummy_fp8_weights` fixture. It is the #67753 patch (8-bit float dummy weights default to `low=-1, high=1`). It also sets `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, because a monkeypatch only reaches an engine in the pytest process.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: replaces the local autouse fixture with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.usefixtures("narrow_dummy_fp8_weights")`. All HiSparse tests already set `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, so they behave as before.
- `tests/compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp1_quant.py`: `test_tp1_fp4_mixed_precision_act_fusion` uses the fixture. It is TP1, so with the engine core in process the model runs in the pytest process, and the patch applies.

## Validation

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (v0.17.2, the pre-commit pin) and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Not yet run on a GPU.** The fusion test needs Blackwell. It runs only in the B200 nightly Fusion E2E Config Sweep step. The HiSparse change only moves code.

## Alternative considered

Giving dense NVFP4 block scales a positive `dummy_weight_value`, as the MoE path does, would fix the root cause for every dummy NVFP4 dense model. It changes dummy-loader behaviour for benchmarks, though, so it is left for a separate discussion with the #67693 author.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Guard cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous is safe only when every rank belongs to
the same NVLink fabric. Without a topology check, unsupported groups can hang
or fail during CUDA memory import. This affects generic symmetric-memory
all-reduce as well as Direct DCP, custom all-reduce, Async TP, GEMM RS/AR, and
the Kimi K3 latent-MoE tail fusion.

This change:

- classifies groups as `INTRA_NODE`, `CROSS_NODE_NVLINK`, or `UNSUPPORTED`;
- reads the fabric UUID and clique ID through vLLM's vendored NVML V2 API
  (`c_nvmlGpuFabricInfoV_t` and `nvmlDeviceGetGpuFabricInfoV`), without spawning
  `nvidia-smi`;
- fails closed when fabric metadata is absent, invalid, or differs across
  ranks;
- applies the topology guard before entering symmetric-memory rendezvous; and
- prevents forced Direct DCP settings from bypassing topology safety.

The legacy `nvmlDeviceGetGpuFabricInfo` structure is not compatible with the
GB300 driver used for validation: it exposed zero clique/state fields. The versioned
V2 call returns correct UUID and clique.

AI assistance was used.

## Test Plan

- Run `git diff --check` and pre-commit on both changed files.
- Run `tests/distributed/test_nvlink_fabric.py` in the GB300 validation image.
- On H100, B200, and GB300 clusters, allocate two nodes, then
  launch eight ranks (four GPUs per node) against exact baseline and patched
  source snapshots using PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`.
- For each topology, inspect raw NVLink fabric metadata, exercise Direct CP in
  forced and automatic modes, initialize `SymmMemCommunicator`, and validate a
  BF16 all-reduce. Each potentially unsafe stage has a 180-second timeout.
- On GB300, test both two nodes within one NVL72 group and two nodes from
  different NVL72 groups.

No model evaluation was run: the change affects collective selection rather
than model numerics. Collective correctness was checked on all eight ranks;
the expected and observed BF16 sum was 36.

## Test Result

| Hardware / topology | Before | Topology after | Direct CP after | Symmetric memory after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100, cross-node | Forced Direct CP was enabled; generic symmetric-memory rendezvous timed out. | `UNSUPPORTED` (null fabric UUID) | **Disabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Disabled**; NCCL fallback correct on 8/8 ranks |
| B200, cross-node | Forced Direct CP was enabled; generic symmetric-memory rendezvous timed out. | `UNSUPPORTED` (null fabric UUID) | **Disabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Disabled**; NCCL fallback correct on 8/8 ranks |
| B200, single-node | Regression check added for this change. | `INTRA_NODE` (null fabric UUID is irrelevant) | **Enabled** in forced and automatic modes | **Enabled**; symmetric-memory all-reduce correct on 4/4 ranks |

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Enable encoder graph capture for Kimi-K3 Vision Tower
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration` on AMD ROCm (MI355X), so the Kimi-K3 vision tower (`MoonViT3dPretrainedModel` + `KimiK25MultiModalProjector`) can be replayed from captured graphs via `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`.

An earlier revision of this PR also added `torch.compile` for the vision tower (`compile_mm_encoder`). That part was dropped after review (thanks @simondanielsson): profiling showed Inductor fuses only norms, residual adds and GELU (full tower 301 -> 275 kernels, about 1% of GPU time), because GEMMs, AITER FMHA and `packed_qk_rope` (about 94% of time) are opaque kernels. The gain comes from graph replay, not fusion.

Related PRs and why this is not a duplicate:

- #53011: avoids eager `torch.compile` in the Kimi K2.5 vision helper (bugfix, not encoder cudagraphs).
- #44394 and #56820: add encoder CUDA graph support for other models (PaddleOCR-VL, Ling-3.0-flash-VL) on the same `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` interface. This PR only implements the interface for Kimi-K3.

No other open PR implements `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` for Kimi-K3. 

## Changes

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/encoder_cudagraph.py`: `KimiK3EncoderCudaGraphMixin` (item specs, item selection, capture inputs, replay buffers, graph and eager forwards). Auto-inferred budgets are capped at 512 tokens; larger inputs use the existing eager path of `EncoderCudaGraphManager`. See [discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63086#discussion_r4440377966) .
- `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py`: test correctness of graph-vs-eager and token cap limit

The feature is opt-in (`cudagraph_mm_encoder`, default off); default behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

### Encoder-level profile (MI355X, full vision tower, 512x512 image)

Wall time per encoder call: eager 7.1 ms, cudagraph replay 4.5 ms. The kernel list is identical; the gain is removed launch overhead and idle gaps between small kernels, so it is largest for small images. Full traces and kernel breakdown: see the profiling section already posted in this description.

### Serving (MI355X, TP=8, 9-point sweep, 3 repetitions per configuration, default config)

A = eager vision tower. D = `cudagraph_mm_encoder=true` only, no manual overrides — budgets auto-infer to `[64, 128, 256, 512]`, i.e. just turning the flag on. Interleaved A/D/A/D/A/D, fresh server boot each. One point, `768x1024`, sits above the 512-token cap so it runs eagerly under D too — a neutral control for the cutoff.

Result: speedup visible both at the serving level and encoder profile.

Note on noise: each sweep point runs 96 prompts (3 reps = ~5h GPU compute), and only one point (256x256 @ conc=16, mean TTFT -13.35%) individually clears the noise band — every other point is inside noise on its own. That's expected: the vision tower runs once per prompt (one image per prompt), so it's a small slice of total request cost, and a clear per-call win in the encoder microbenchmark (7.1ms eager -> 4.5ms graphed) shows up as a small, only-geomean-resolvable gain at the serving level. The geomean (not any single point) is the evidence for a real effect.

| metric | D vs A (geomean) | noise floor |
|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT | -3.92% ± 1.60 | ≤4.0%/point — reliable |
| Median TTFT | -0.87% ± 5.39 | up to 25%/point — directional only |
| Throughput | +3.12% ± 1.85 | ≤7.7%/point |
| TPOT | -2.83%/-2.11% | expected flat; within noise, decode path untouched |

Above-cap control (`768x1024`, eager under D): throughput +2.71%, mean TTFT +3.30% — flat/noisy as expected, confirms traffic above the cutoff isn't regressed.

</details>


### Accuracy

| Metric | A (eager) | D (cudagraph only) | D vs A |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| MMMU score (N=900, single run) | 0.6734 | 0.6678 | -0.8% (-0.56 points) |

MMMU was evaluated once per configuration on N=900 questions: D (cudagraph only) **0.6678**, against the eager baseline A. 0.6% difference is not significant, no regression.
Output equivalence of graph replay vs the eager vision tower is also covered by the unit tests below.

<details>

```bash
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \

    --max-model-len 131072 \

    --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512 \

    --async-scheduling \
    --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
    --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \
    --mm-processor-kwargs '{"min_pixels": 65536, "max_pixels": 16777216}' \
    --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
```

where `<IMAGE>` is based on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-76c6f3f2a95f6049657db1e513133b824a5c8175` with the changes of this PR. The AITER, quick-reduce and `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` settings are part of the standard Kimi-K3 serving recipe used for all configurations (not specific to this PR).

Baseline A is the same command without `cudagraph_mm_encoder`, budgets and max-items.

</details>

## Scope and limitations

- ROCm only; the NVIDIA model is unchanged. Deduplicating the encoder-graph methods between `amd/model.py` and `nvidia/model.py` into a common mixin is planned as a follow-up PR once this merges.
- Default auto-inferred budgets are capped at 512 tokens; larger inputs run eagerly. See [discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63086#discussion_r4440377966)
- Serving statistics: 3 repetitions on a single node, 96 prompts/point (32 at conc=1/4, 256 at conc=64), fixed seeds per point. Geomean deltas are reliable (stdev ≤1.9%); per-point deltas are noisier — below ~4% for mean TTFT, ~8% for throughput/TPOT, ~25% for median TTFT isn't distinguishable from noise. The vision tower runs once per prompt, so a real per-call improvement is a small fraction of total request time and only resolves at the geomean level, not per point.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Drop the stale config read from the FlashInfer indexer builder
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `MiniMaxM3IndexerFlashInferMetadataBuilder` (added in #66018) still reads the legacy `text_config.sparse_attention_config` dict, which the upstream `MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig` adopted in #61813 no longer exposes. Constructing the builder raises `AttributeError` on SM90 and SM120/SM121, where the FlashInfer MSA indexer is selected. This PR removes that read. ## Claims - The FlashInfer indexer builder constructs again with the upstream MiniMax-M3 config. - `test_flashinfer_indexer_impl_matches_triton` passes again on SM121 (it fails on `main`). - No behavior change otherwise: `local_blocks` comes from the same config field, through the impl instead of the builder. ## Validation DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, driver 580.178.04), `main` at 6d3eba027 (the two touched files are unchanged at 1c675c6868), precompiled cu132 wheel, torch 2.14.0, flashinfer 0.7.3, transformers 5.22.2. ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py -k flashinfer_indexer -v pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py pre-commit run --files vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/indexer_flashinfer.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py ``` `-k flashinfer_indexer`: | tree | result | |---|---| | `main` | 4 failed, `common/indexer.py:255`: `'Qwen3Config' object has no attribute 'index_n_heads'` (stale test setup) | | `main` + the test change | 4 failed, `indexer_flashinfer.py:78`: `'Qwen3Config' object has no attribute 'sparse_attention_config'` | | this PR | 4 passed | | this PR with `force_end = 0` | 2 failed (the `local_blocks=1` cases), 2 passed, so the test covers the value now taken from the impl | Whole file with this PR: 166 passed, 103 skipped. `pre-commit`: passed. With the `config.json` of `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` and `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` loaded through `get_config`, on the same GPU `minimax_m3_use_flashinfer_msa` passes and `select_indexer_impl_cls` returns `MiniMaxM3IndexerFlashInferImpl` for bf16 and fp8 index caches. Constructing its builder fails on `main` with ``` AttributeError: 'MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig' object has no attribute 'sparse_attention_config' ``` and succeeds with this PR. End to end on the same GPU: a tiny dummy-weight MiniMax-M3 (the config from `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_index_cache_overrides.py`, which is ROCm-only) started through `LLM(..., load_format="dummy")`, two 2304-token prompts, 4 greedy tokens each. | tree | result | |---|---| | `main` | engine does not start: `create_metadata_builders` -> `indexer_flashinfer.py:78` -> `AttributeError: 'MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig' object has no attribute 'sparse_attention_config'` -> `Engine core initialization failed` | | this PR | engine starts, logs `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected FlashInfer MSA (proxy score + top-k)`, and generates for both prompts | The script passes `attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}` for the dense layers, because FLASH_ATTN from the cu132 wheel does not load on this machine's 580 driver (#67177). That is unrelated to this change.
e2e_m3_dummy.py (run as python e2e_m3_dummy.py TRITON_ATTN) ```python """End-to-end engine start + generation for a tiny dummy-weight MiniMax-M3 (same recipe as tests/models/minimax_m3/test_index_cache_overrides.py, which is ROCm-only), to reach the FlashInfer indexer builder on this GPU.""" import math import sys import tempfile from transformers import MiniMaxM3VLConfig from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="m3tiny-") MiniMaxM3VLConfig( architectures=["MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM"], text_config={ "num_hidden_layers": 5, "hidden_size": 128, "dense_intermediate_size": 256, "num_attention_heads": 1, "num_key_value_heads": 1, "head_dim": 128, "vocab_size": 256, "bos_token_id": 1, "eos_token_id": 2, "max_position_embeddings": 4096, "mlp_layer_types": ["dense"] * 5, "layer_types": ["full_attention"] * 3 + ["minimax_m3_sparse"] * 2, "index_n_heads": 1, }, ).save_pretrained(tmp) if __name__ == "__main__": extra = {} if len(sys.argv) > 1: extra["backend"] = sys.argv[1] llm = LLM( tmp, load_format="dummy", skip_tokenizer_init=True, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096, block_size=128, max_num_seqs=1, max_num_batched_tokens=4096, kv_cache_memory_bytes=64 * 1024 * 1024, enforce_eager=True, enable_prefix_caching=False, attention_config={"indexer_kv_dtype": "bf16", **extra}, generation_config="vllm", ) for offset in (0, 37): tokens = [3 + (i + offset) % 250 for i in range(2304)] out = llm.generate( [{"prompt_token_ids": tokens}], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=4, ignore_eos=True, logprobs=5), use_tqdm=False, )[0].outputs[0] vals = [p.logprob for row in out.logprobs for p in row.values()] assert len(out.token_ids) == 4 and all(math.isfinite(v) for v in vals) print("E2E_GENERATED offset", offset, "token_ids", list(out.token_ids)) print("E2E_OK") ```
Not run: a released checkpoint. They are 252-854 GB (172 GB for the smallest quantized one I found), more than the 121 GB of this machine. SM90 was not tested. The end-to-end run uses dummy weights, so no eval was run; the change does not alter model output. ## Details `MiniMaxM3VLTextConfig.__post_init__` pops `sparse_attention_config` and maps it to flat `index_*` fields, so the attribute does not exist on a loaded config. #66018 was opened before #61813 merged and landed after it, which is how the legacy read got in. The impl already receives `local_blocks` from the model (`local_blocks=config.index_local_blocks`), which is what the MSA and Triton indexers use. `forward` now uses `self.local_blocks`, and the builder's copy is removed (`__init__`, the metadata field, two imports). The test sets `index_n_heads` instead of the legacy dict. CI did not catch this: `test_flashinfer_indexer_impl_matches_triton` needs SM90 or SM120/SM121, and the steps that run this file use L4 and B200 (skipped) or H100 with `-k prefill_sparse_attention_correctness` (deselected). The second commit adds the test to that H100 step's `-k` filter and lists `common/indexer.py` and `nvidia/indexer_flashinfer.py` as its dependencies. I could not run it on SM90, so this PR's own H100 run is the first check of that path; on SM121 the new filter selects 8 tests and all pass. Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR mentions `indexer_flashinfer` or this `AttributeError` (searched 2026-11-12), and #66018 has no follow-up commits. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, tests, and review. The human submitter reviewed the changes and authorized submission. The validation results above were obtained with AI assistance. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Disable expanded DeepEP v2 dispatch in all execution modes
commits.pr_body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This PR is a duplicate of and supersedes #59337.** It is opened from
> `neuralmagic/vllm` because the original PR branch is in a fork where the
> submitter does not have write access. The original description, rationale
> and validation history are copied below, followed by validation on the
> replacement branch.

## Replacement Branch Update

Current head `47ba135367d78e666d25daa2c322e2f5f1d7369b` includes merge
`c6f2e79c6b` with `origin/main` at `9ad0029883` and the final
`test_moe.py` receiver-signature compatibility fix.

- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed for all seven changed files, including
  Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, test-tethering and docstring checks;
  `git diff --check` also passed.
- Full DeepEP v2 test set: **1548 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed**. The 16 skips
  require FlashInfer TRTLLM on SM100; validation used H200/SM90 GPUs.
- DeepEP v2 async-finalize suite in the requested environment with NCCL 2.30.7:
  **6 passed**.
- Previously failing `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py` set on two H200 GPUs:
  **191 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed** (891 deselected; 2m45s).

## Purpose

DeepEP v2 currently selects expanded dispatch and CPU synchronization from `enforce_eager`. Use `do_expand=False` and `do_cpu_sync=False` for every forward so eager execution, warmup and CUDA graph capture share the same dispatch contract.

Remove the constructor flag and unused expanded-layout receiver code. Preserve DP-wide, sequence-parallel-aware receive-capacity buckets, padding masking and GPU receive metadata. Allow preparation without a forward context by falling back to the input shape.

Expanded dispatch needs an expert backend that consumes grouped rows efficiently. Enabling it for large prefills is deferred to a backend-specific follow-up with rank-coordinated policy, tuning and serving validation. Capacity-based allocations may use more memory than the previous synchronized eager path; this PR claims no general speedup or memory reduction.

Duplicate-work check: open DeepEP PRs were inspected. #51589 proposes opt-in adaptive prefill dispatch; this change makes non-expanded dispatch unconditional. It does not duplicate #50511's padding fix or #59687's SP buffer sizing fix. Future expanded-prefill work should coordinate with #51589.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review and validation. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line, running relevant tests, and defending the change.

Exercise prepare/finalize contracts and BF16/FP8 expert outputs across eager execution, capture/replay and return to eager. Validate exact 8k/16k synthetic prefills, full GSM8K, and non-overloaded 8k-input/1k-output serving with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Mistral Large 4 fails to start on ROCm on `main`: every worker crashes at model init because the AMD `MistralIndexerCache` is still abstract. #61452 replaced `AttentionLayerBase.get_kv_cache_spec` with the abstract `get_kv_cache_config`, and #64534 (Mistral Large 4) merged a day later still implementing only `get_kv_cache_spec`.

## Claims

- Fixes the ROCm startup crash `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MistralIndexerCache without an implementation for abstract method 'get_kv_cache_config'` for Mistral Large 4.
- No behavior change otherwise: the indexer cache spec is identical to before, now wrapped in a `KVCacheLayerConfig` under `FullAttentionManager`, as `DeepseekV32IndexerCache` does.

## Validation

**Regression test:** on ROCm, `test_indexer_k_cache_write` in `tests/models/mistral/test_fused_ops.py` now builds the real `MistralIndexerCache` and checks that the page its `get_kv_cache_config()` requests matches the cache the kernels are tested on. Run on MI300 (gfx942):

<details>
<summary>Without fix</summary>

```
$ pytest -v -s tests/models/mistral/test_fused_ops.py -k test_indexer_k_cache_write
E               TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MistralIndexerCache without an implementation for abstract method 'get_kv_cache_config'
36 failed, 32 deselected in 19.85s
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>With fix</summary>

```
$ pytest -v -s tests/models/mistral/test_fused_ops.py
65 passed, 3 skipped in 9.98s
SKIPPED [3] test_fused_ops.py:184: the fused_indexer_q_rope_quant reference is CUDA-only
```
</details>

**End-to-end** on 8x MI300 (gfx942), TP=8:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 64000 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser mistral --mm-encoder-tp-mode data
```

<details>
<summary>Without fix: all 8 workers fail at model init</summary>

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=978) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]   File ".../vllm/models/mistral/mistral_large4/amd/model.py", line 89, in __init__
(Worker_TP0 pid=978) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]     self.self_attn = MistralMLAAttention(
(Worker_TP0 pid=978) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]   File ".../vllm/models/mistral/amd/attention.py", line 131, in __init__
(Worker_TP0 pid=978) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]     MistralIndexer(
(Worker_TP0 pid=978) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]   File ".../vllm/models/mistral/amd/indexer.py", line 163, in __init__
(Worker_TP0 pid=978) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091]     self.k_cache = MistralIndexerCache(
(Worker_TP0 pid=978) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1091] TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MistralIndexerCache without an implementation for abstract method 'get_kv_cache_config'
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```
</details>

With fix: server starts and serves requests</summary>


## Details

**Root cause:** a merge race. #61452 (merged Nov 12) made `get_kv_cache_config` the abstract KV-cache hook on `AttentionLayerBase` and migrated every existing layer, but #64534 (merged Nov 13) was developed against the old interface. Nothing in vLLM calls `get_kv_cache_spec` any more, so the old method was dead code and the class could not be instantiated.

**Fix:** rename the method in `vllm/models/mistral/amd/indexer.py` and return `FullAttentionManager.layer_config(spec)`, matching `DeepseekV32IndexerCache`, which this cache mirrors. The ROCm block-size check is unchanged.

**CI:** the extended test runs in the existing `:amd: (MI355) Mistral Large 4` step (`pytest -v -s models/mistral`). CI can't run the full 1T-parameter model, so end-to-end coverage is the manual run above.
