commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] OCP MX emulation: dequantize only the routed experts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On GPUs without native OCP MX support (e.g. MI250X), MXFP4/MXFP6 MoE layers run through `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts`, which dequantizes every local expert to bf16/fp16 on every forward. A decode batch usually routes to a small fraction of the experts, so this PR dequantizes only the routed ones when they are at most a quarter of the local experts. Related, touching the same class but not this path: #43983 (oracle test coverage), #52868 (`a2_scale` forwarding).

Credit: @ekuznetsov139 had the same idea earlier in #40055 (single-token decode; on MI325 it took Qwen3-235B from about 4 to 21 tok/s). Its capturable single-token path is folded in here (5a4baceea, co-authored by him).

## Claims

- When a batch routes to at most a quarter of the local experts, `apply` gathers the routed experts' packed weights and scales, dequantizes only those, and renumbers `topk_ids` onto the gathered set. For multi-token batches this uses `torch.unique(..., return_inverse=True)`. For a single token (from #40055) it uses a sort of the token's ids and an argsort, so shapes are static and the path also runs under CUDA-graph capture.
- The output is unchanged when both paths select the same Triton tile config: each token is multiplied by the same dequantized expert weights. Tuned config files are keyed by expert count, and the routed path looks up the gathered count, so on a GPU with a tuned file for the full shape the full path may use a tuned tile while the routed path uses the default one, and the outputs can then differ by rounding. vLLM has no tuned configs for MI250X, so both paths use the default config there; the test checks bit-identity with `torch.equal`.
- Past a quarter, for an empty batch, for multi-token batches under CUDA-graph capture, and with an `expert_map` (EP), LoRA experts or w1/w2 biases, the existing full dequantization runs unchanged.
- One MoE layer of a 256-expert MXFP4 model at TP8 on MI250X: 6.6 ms per call before, 1.5 ms with 8 routed experts (c=1), 2.3 ms with 31 (c=4). This is a microbenchmark; see Validation.

## Validation

**Microbenchmark, MI250X (gfx90a), one MoE layer** of a large 256-expert MXFP4 MoE model at TP8, measured on a GCD that was busy with other work (the routed rows include the gather):

| routed experts | time per call |
|---|---|
| all (main) | 6.6 ms |
| 8 (c=1 decode) | 1.5 ms |
| 31 (c=4) | 2.3 ms |
| 100 (gather forced) | 6.2 ms |
| 225 (gather forced) | 15.5 ms |

The last two rows were measured with the gather forced, to pick the threshold. With 256 experts the threshold is 64, so this PR sends both to the full path. The layer output was bit-identical in every row (default tile configs on both paths).

**No end-to-end number.** This change has not been served end to end on this base. Before the change, c=1 decode of that model (TP8 x PP3) ran at about 2.4 tok/s.

**Test**, `test_emulation_routed_dequant_moe_forward_is_bit_identical` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py` (ROCm only, using that file's `ROCM_AVAILABLE` skip): a real MXFP4 emulation MoE forward with 32 experts. A spy on `_dequantize_weights` records how many experts each call dequantizes; the test runs once normally, once with the capture flag patched on (only the single-token case stays routed), and once with the full path forced, and compares outputs with `torch.equal`. Three cases: 4 tokens routed to 5 experts (routed path), 5 tokens routed to 9 experts, past the threshold of 8 (full path), and 1 token routed to 2 experts (single-token path).

<details>
<summary>commands and output (1x MI250X, gfx90a, main 8e2beaa3b)</summary>

```
$ pytest kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k test_emulation_routed_dequant_moe_forward_is_bit_identical     # with this change
3 passed, 181 deselected in 44.74s

# without (non-test files reverted to main)
E       AssertionError: assert [32, 32] == [5, 5]
E       AttributeError: <class '...OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts'> has no attribute '_routed_experts'
E       AssertionError: assert [32, 32] == [2, 2]
3 failed, 181 deselected in 9.72s
# (the past-threshold case fails on main only because the test patches the new helper)

# real CUDA-graph capture of one token through apply(), replayed with other expert ids
dequant sizes during capture: [2, 2]
replay ids=[30, 2]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[5, 17]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[0, 31]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[9, 9]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
replay ids=[12, 3]: equal_to_full_dequant=True maxdiff=0
```

Rebased on main `db3b0f0fa`: ruff, typos, SPDX and mypy (3.11 hook) are clean (ruff re-run after the fold-in). The test is skipped on CPU and CUDA hosts.
</details>

**Not tested:** MXFP6 schemes (same code path; only the dequantization function differs); end-to-end throughput.

## Details

**Host sync.** Outside graph capture, multi-token batches add one `torch.unique` per MoE layer per forward, which synchronizes with the host. It runs before the threshold check, so batches that end up on the full path pay it too. Under capture, multi-token batches take the full path, as they do today. The single-token path (from #40055) has no host sync and a fixed size (`topk` slots), so batch-1 decode graphs capture it; a repeated id there would only cost a duplicate gather.

**Threshold.** A quarter of the local experts is where, on MI250X, the gather and renumbering cost about as much as the dequantization they save (the 100-expert row above is already at parity with the full path). It is a constant in `apply`, not a config knob.

**Why not EP/LoRA/bias.** With an `expert_map` the ids are global and would need remapping before the gather; LoRA and biases index per-expert tensors that the gather does not cover. These cases keep the full path rather than growing this change.
AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Quantization][Perf] Fuse the block Hadamard input rotation into AITER's MXFP4 activation quant
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, `mxfp4_hadamard32` layers on AITER's ASM MXFP4 GEMM now rotate their input inside the activation quant ([ROCm/aiter#6734](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6734)) instead of in a separate PyTorch kernel, which recovers the 6–12% serving throughput that #62750's rotation costs on Qwen3.8-2.4T.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "hadamard mxfp4" and "hadamard rotation aiter"; #65398 adds a MoE variant of the online scheme and does not fuse the rotation.

## Claims

- TP8 serving output throughput is within 0.6% of plain RTN `mxfp4` at concurrency 4, 64 and 256. With #62750's PyTorch rotation it is 6.0–12.4% lower.
- Per layer, the fused rotation adds 0–5% to quant + GEMM, where the PyTorch rotation adds 70–170%.
- The output matches the PyTorch rotation up to bf16 rounding, so #62750's accuracy results carry over.

## Validation

8x MI355X, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Quark MXFP4, TP8. vLLM nightly `df3bd094` plus the arm's diff, with ROCm/aiter#6734 ported to its AITER 0.1.25. All arms put the GDN projections (`in_proj_qkvz`, `out_proj`) and the shared experts on online MXFP4 (322 layers) and differ only in the GDN projections' scheme.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1 AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --load-format dummy \
  --compilation-config '{"splitting_ops": [], "pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache": true, "enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion": true, "fuse_allreduce_rms": true}}' \
  --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "mxfp4_hadamard32", "*linear_attn.in_proj_z": "mxfp4_hadamard32", "*linear_attn.out_proj": "mxfp4_hadamard32"}'

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --ignore-eos --max-concurrency {4,64,256} --num-prompts {32,256,1024} --seed {1,2}
```

The RTN arm uses `"mxfp4"` for the three GDN targets.

**Serving**, mean of 2 repeats (repeats differ by up to 1.6%), fresh caches per arm:

| GDN projections | Output tok/s c=4 | c=64 | c=256 | Mean TPOT ms c=4 | c=64 | c=256 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTN `mxfp4` | 373.0 | 1807.1 | 4028.3 | 10.45 | 34.09 | 60.91 |
| `mxfp4_hadamard32`, PyTorch rotation (#62750) | 326.9 (-12.4%) | 1694.4 (-6.2%) | 3787.7 (-6.0%) | 11.94 | 36.23 | 64.86 |
| `mxfp4_hadamard32`, fused (this PR) | 371.3 (-0.5%) | 1796.6 (-0.6%) | 4024.2 (-0.1%) | 10.50 | 34.21 | 61.09 |

**Per layer**, quant + GEMM in µs, one GPU, CUDA graph:

| M | `in_proj_qkvz` plain | PyTorch rotation | Fused | `out_proj` plain | PyTorch rotation | Fused |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 7.2 | 15.3 | 7.4 | 5.3 | 10.9 | 5.0 |
| 16 | 9.5 | 17.1 | 9.2 | 5.4 | 12.6 | 5.6 |
| 256 | 14.7 | 28.1 | 15.0 | 8.0 | 17.6 | 8.5 |
| 1024 | 29.3 | 65.1 | 29.6 | 16.9 | 32.5 | 17.0 |
| 8192 | 170.6 | 459.1 | 175.7 | 83.5 | 155.5 | 88.0 |

**Accuracy.** On the same inputs, the fused and PyTorch rotations give the same relative error against the unquantized GEMM to five digits at every M from 1024 to 16384. Up to 0.07% of output elements differ (fp32 butterfly vs bf16 matmul, then the same bf16 rounding before FP4). #62750 measured this rotation on Qwen3.8-2.4T with real weights (thinking on, paired seeds, exact McNemar):

| Eval | BF16 → `mxfp4_hadamard32` | Fixed / broken | p | Length vs BF16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K, 12 reps | 96.34 → 96.13 | +125 / -158 | 0.057 | 1.026 [1.000, 1.052] |
| GPQA Diamond, 5 reps | 92.3 → 93.1 | +20 / -12 | 0.22 | 0.940 [0.904, 0.977] |

**Unit tests** (MI355X, stock nightly `be47189f` with AITER 0.1.29), 91 passed, 4 skipped, with and without `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py \
  tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py tests/v1/determinism/test_mx_linear_batch_invariant.py
```

`test_input_hadamard.py` fails if the ASM path stops fusing, if the Triton or emulation path starts, or if the wrapper rotates twice. `test_online_mxfp4.py` fails if the fake `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` drifts from the op again.

## Details

- `InputHadamardFusable` (in `input_hadamard.py`) is an opt-in mixin with `fuse_input_hadamard(layer, size) -> bool`. `InputHadamardLinearMethod` still rotates the weight, and skips its input rotation when the wrapped method is fusable and returns `True`. Online MXFP4, `QuarkLinearMethod` and Quark OCP MX inherit it and forward the call to their `MxFp4LinearKernel`.
- `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` fuses only on its ASM GEMM path with size 32, and passes `hadamard_rotate=True` to the HIP quant. The Triton path keeps the PyTorch rotation. The server logs `... rotates its input by the 32-wide Hadamard matrix itself.` once per method.
- The ASM path is used only for (N, K) in AITER's tuned a4w4 config. `out_proj` is tuned today; ROCm/aiter#7441 adds the `in_proj_qkvz` (N=4608, K=8192) config that the numbers above include.
- Also fixes the fake impl of `gemm_with_dynamic_quant`, whose signature had drifted from the op.

**Limitations and CI gaps.** Serving used dummy weights, and accuracy was measured on #62750's unfused path; the fused path's equivalence rests on the per-element comparison above. No CI job runs these tests until the Quantization jobs are re-enabled (#66900, #66672). The MI355 job will then cover the fused path: the AITER cases turn AITER on themselves, since CI does not set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Prevent NVSHMEM IB transport setup hang in DBO GSM8K tests
commits.pr_body:
#### Overview
Fixes the intermittent NVSHMEM startup hang in `test_dbo_v2_features_gsm8k` on single-node multi-GPU runs (fixes part of #67307).

#### Root Cause
When the two GPUs sit on different CPU NUMA sockets, NVSHMEM and DeepEP attempt to initialize InfiniBand Queue Pairs across host NICs (`ibv_modify_qp failed`), causing the background test server to hang indefinitely until the CI timeout.

#### Fix
Pass `NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none` and `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST=none` to `RemoteOpenAIServer` in `tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py`. This keeps NVSHMEM strictly on the local NVLink fabric and off host NICs for single-node execution, following the identical pattern merged in #61695 and #66207.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Correct the batch-invariance comment on Hopper/Blackwell split-k
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The comment in `enable_batch_invariant_mode` for SM90/SM100 says that split-k is the only source of batch variance on those GPUs and that the cuBLAS workspace config disables it. That is not accurate for every shape: with split-k disabled, some narrow shapes such as MoE router projections are still not batch invariant in cuBLAS, which is why #35404 routes unquantized Linear layers to the Triton `linear_batch_invariant` on every CUDA device. The comment as written suggests cuBLAS is enough on Hopper/Blackwell (it led me to propose the opposite in #65569). This changes the comment only; no code changes.

## Evidence

From the discussion in #65569 (raw data linked there): under batch-invariant mode's settings, the gpt-oss-20b router (32 x 2880) differs between a row computed alone and inside a batch on H100 and H200, and on H100 narrow widths (N <= 96 at K = 2880/4096/5120, and widths 97-127 that are not multiples of 8) also differ, while wide projections pass.

## Test Plan

Comment-only change.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Fail pulls from a lost prefill worker
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a prefill worker dies, the Mooncake decoder does not notice. Its pull waits up to `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT + 60` = 540 s for P's reply while holding the request's KV blocks, because ZMQ reconnects silently instead of reporting the lost peer. D also keeps the dead worker's address cached, so the requests queued behind send their pulls there and wait another 540 s. Under load, D's KV stays full of requests that can never finish.

This PR fails a pull as soon as its connection is lost, and makes D look P up again. It is the decoder-side counterpart of #64193.

## Claims

- **P process dies:** the requests waiting on it fail within 2–4 s, instead of after 545 s plus a second 540 s wave.
- **P frozen or unreachable:** they fail once heartbeats or the existing timeouts expire, all within 102 s.
- No change for a live P and no new option. Failures follow `kv_load_failure_policy`.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake*.py` → 750 passed, 5 skipped. 4 more cases hit Hugging Face Hub fetch errors and pass on rerun.
- The new test runs a ZMQ ROUTER in a subprocess that takes the pull and never answers. The ROUTER is then killed, frozen with `SIGSTOP`, or never listening. All three cases time out on main and pass in about 1 s with this PR.
- This PR also fixes `test_mooncake_stats.py::test_expired_request_bumps_counter`, which has been broken since #64193.

`pre-commit` passes.

**End to end:**
- Setup: 2× A800, DeepSeek-MoE-16B, TP=1 per side, `kv_lease_duration=30`.
- Load: 128 requests at 2.4× D's KV capacity.
- Failure: P's process group gets the signal at t≈41 s. Times are measured from the signal.

| | main, `SIGKILL` | this PR, `SIGKILL` | this PR, `SIGSTOP` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stranded requests fail | 545 s, then 1,084 s | 2–4 s | 12–102 s |
| D's KV usage below 50% | 556 s | 5.5 s | 109 s |
| Requests ok / failed | 53 / 75 | 54 / 74 | 53 / 75 |

## Details

**Root cause**
1. D allocates blocks for a request, sends a pull to P's ZMQ ROUTER, and waits for the reply.
2. If P dies, D's DEALER silently reconnects, or keeps retrying a refused connect, so the wait runs to the 540 s timeout. The reply can never arrive: the DEALER has no routing id, so P's ROUTER drops replies addressed to a lost connection.
3. `_remote_agents` is never invalidated, so later requests pull from the same dead address.

**Fix**
- D monitors each pull socket for `EVENT_DISCONNECTED | EVENT_CONNECT_RETRIED`. On either event, it fails the pull through `_handle_failed_recv`, and drops the cached addresses of every engine that lists this worker. Later requests then query the bootstrap server again: a dead P fails at once, and a restarted P is found.
- ZMTP heartbeats (2 s / 10 s, as in `kv_offload/tiering/p2p/control/zmq.py`) make a frozen or unreachable P drop the connection too. libzmq applies them only when they are set before `connect()`, so `make_zmq_socket` takes them as arguments.

**Tradeoffs and limitations**
- A pull whose connect hits a transient network error now fails, where ZMQ would have retried it.
- Frozen P: pulls sent before D notices wait for ZMQ's 30 s handshake timeout. Requests queued after that wait for the bootstrap query to time out (3 × `VLLM_MOONCAKE_CONNECTOR_TIMEOUT`), hence the 102 s.
- Cost: one inproc monitor socket per pull, about 30 µs.

#35943 and #37745 reported this hang and were closed as not planned. No open PR covers it.

**AI assistance:** written with Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line, ran all tests and experiments above, and can answer for the design.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Set the CPU tier up in the background under async_init
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Milestone 1 of #66570. Builds on #66391; only the last two commits are new.

With `"async_init": true`, workers map the CPU region and return right away. A background thread then pre-faults and pins it, while the engine serves without offloading. Offloading turns on once every worker reports ready.

- The setup thread switches itself to relaxed capture mode, so pinning can't invalidate a CUDA graph capture. That race is what reverted #45850. If the mode can't be set, setup fails and offloading stays off.
- It pins one small call at a time (a worker slot, or whole rows up to 8 MiB) and sleeps `async_init_pin_pace` (default 2.0) times each call's duration after it. Back-to-back registrations hold a driver lock and stall serving.
- Readiness goes through the connector's existing worker metadata, so nothing outside the offloading connector changes. Once #62337 lands, this gate moves to the core.
- If setup fails, offloading stays off and the engine keeps serving.
- CUDA only; other platforms set up synchronously. Off by default.

This covers `CPUOffloadingSpec`. `TieringOffloadingSpec` ignores the option with a warning until the follow-up. #54578 proposes the same key with a different design; the two need to be reconciled.

## Results

Startup to `/health` OK, with the Tiering follow-up on top:

| Setup | Sync | async_init |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3, 16 H100 (4 pods), 280 GiB/rank | 439 s | 334 s |
| Qwen3-8B (dummy weights), TP=4, 1,250 GiB | 241.5 s | 57-61 s |

On GLM, pre-fault (117 s) and pinning (12 s) leave the critical path. That run used an earlier build without pacing; pinning started after healthy, so the healthy time is the same.

Request latency while pinning runs (Qwen3-8B, 1,250 GiB, one 9 MiB slot per call):

| Pinning | Worst latency | Time to pin |
|---|---|---|
| Unpaced (3 runs) | 0.4-1.4 s | 23 s |
| Paced 2x | 0.18 s | 51-55 s |

Latency before pinning started was 0.084 s.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
```

Plus, on 2x H100 80GB at this head: a standalone capture race, and `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --tensor-parallel-size 2` with an 8 GiB CPU tier and a GPU cache small enough to evict.

## Test Result

Unit suites on H100, against #66391 at `b052cf92f3`:

- `tests/v1/kv_offload`: 1017 passed, 6 skipped (1011 before).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector`: 742 passed (740 before).

Capture race, 200 global-mode graph captures while a second thread calls `cudaHostRegister`:

| Second thread | Captures failed |
|---|---|
| default capture mode | 200 / 200 (`cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated`) |
| relaxed, as the setup thread does | 0 / 200 across 199,103 registrations |

End to end (Qwen3-0.6B, TP=2, 8 GiB tier):

- Sync and `async_init` stored the same 4.07 GB, loaded the same 360 MB back from CPU for an evicted prompt (3,136 of 3,162 tokens cached) and returned the same text.
- With `async_init_pin_pace=30`, pinning took 16-18 s per rank and overlapped the second graph-capture pass; both passes completed. Offloading turned on 11 s into a 22 s request; the chunks it skipped were stored afterwards (462 MB) and loaded back after eviction.
- Injected failure: with the capture-mode switch removed, `cudaHostRegister` fails during warmup and the engine does not come up.
- `TieringOffloadingSpec` with `async_init` logs the warning, sets up synchronously and serves the same results.

The 8 GiB tier is too small to show the startup gain; the Results above cover that.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][Perf] Add H100 BF16 batch-invariant matmul configs for gpt-oss
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Related to #65569 and the batch-invariance performance tracker #27433. Add Hopper BF16 persistent-matmul configs, in the format of #62219, for the bf16 Linear shapes that popular models send through `linear_batch_invariant` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4.1, gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b. In GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1 everything else is FP8/FP4 and uses other kernels, so the bf16 layers are the routers, the sparse-attention indexer projections, DeepSeek-V4.1's compressor and `lm_head` (per rank at TP=8 and TP=4). gpt-oss-20b's and gpt-oss-120b's unquantized attention, routers and `lm_head` run this kernel since #35404. The Triton path is unchanged; nothing is routed to cuBLAS.

## Claims

- Invariance: each shape uses one `BLOCK_K` across all M buckets. A row multiplied alone vs. inside batches of M = 1..1024 and every 16th M up to 8192 (first 8, last 8 and 4 middle rows): 0 of 438,030 rows differ over all 15 shapes.
- Kernel speed on H100: the tuned configs are 1.08x-3.04x faster than the default config at every bucket of every shape (table below).
- End to end on one H100 (`vllm bench serve`, 3 alternating rounds, raw logs in the comments below): gpt-oss-20b: decode-heavy output throughput +4.3% over main (faster in 3 of 3 rounds; loss against batch invariance off 22.8% -> 19.5%), prefill-heavy request throughput +2.4% (faster in 2 of 3 rounds); gpt-oss-120b: decode-heavy output throughput +1.9% over main (faster in 3 of 3 rounds; loss against batch invariance off 22.1% -> 20.6%), prefill-heavy request throughput +0.9% (faster in 2 of 3 rounds). The gains are modest because gpt-oss's MoE experts use another kernel; the same will hold for GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1, where only the layers above are bf16.
- New test `test_hopper_tuned_linear_batch_invariance` checks config selection and exact first/last-row equality on both sides of every bucket boundary for all 15 shapes. `tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py` on H100: 50 passed (15 new cases).

## Shapes and kernel times

Speedup over the default config / time relative to cuBLAS, at M = 1, 32, 256, 2048:

| Model | Layer | (N, K) | BLOCK_K | M=1 | M=32 | M=256 | M=2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3 | MoE router | (256, 6144) | 128 | 2.53x / 1.84 | 2.57x / 1.66 | 2.59x / 1.38 | 1.99x / 1.14 |
| GLM-5.3 | indexer `wk_weights_proj` | (160, 6144) | 128 | 2.51x / 1.95 | 2.59x / 1.72 | 2.55x / 1.61 | 2.08x / 1.08 |
| GLM-5.3 | `lm_head`, TP=8 | (19360, 6144) | 64 | 2.57x / 1.02 | 2.21x / 1.02 | 1.27x / 1.26 | 1.44x / 0.98 |
| GLM-5.3 | `lm_head`, TP=4 | (38720, 6144) | 64 | 2.12x / 1.00 | 1.86x / 1.03 | 1.26x / 1.13 | 1.30x / 1.17 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | MoE router | (384, 5120) | 128 | 2.48x / 1.56 | 2.50x / 1.41 | 2.33x / 1.37 | 1.72x / 1.23 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | indexer `weights_proj` | (32, 5120) | 128 | 2.37x / 1.78 | 2.37x / 1.57 | 2.38x / 1.47 | 2.54x / 1.09 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | indexer `wk` | (128, 512) | 128 | 1.41x / 1.03 | 1.45x / 0.98 | 1.48x / 0.97 | 1.32x / 0.98 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | compressor `fused_wkv_wgate` | (1024, 5120) | 128 | 2.57x / 1.42 | 2.57x / 1.28 | 2.38x / 1.12 | 1.20x / 1.21 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | `lm_head`, TP=8 | (16160, 5120) | 64 | 2.51x / 0.95 | 2.20x / 0.96 | 1.34x / 1.05 | 1.41x / 1.08 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 | `lm_head`, TP=4 | (32320, 5120) | 64 | 2.33x / 0.96 | 2.02x / 0.97 | 1.38x / 1.02 | 1.37x / 0.99 |
| gpt-oss-20b | qkv_proj | (5120, 2880) | 128 | 2.83x / 1.06 | 2.47x / 1.07 | 1.13x / 1.37 | 1.14x / 1.29 |
| gpt-oss-20b | o_proj | (2880, 4096) | 128 | 3.04x / 1.09 | 2.57x / 1.05 | 1.64x / 1.21 | 1.08x / 1.50 |
| gpt-oss-20b | `lm_head` | (201088, 2880) | 64 | 2.56x / 0.96 | 2.07x / 0.98 | 1.41x / 1.04 | 1.26x / 1.03 |
| gpt-oss-20b | MoE router | (32, 2880) | 128 | 2.13x / 1.27 | 2.07x / 1.19 | 2.08x / 1.17 | 2.51x / 0.99 |
| gpt-oss-120b | MoE router | (128, 2880) | 128 | 2.12x / 1.30 | 2.14x / 1.16 | 2.06x / 1.14 | 1.89x / 1.13 |

Shapes were read from the GLM-5.3 checkpoint and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's safetensors headers and matched to vLLM's model code (`GateLinear` falls back to `ReplicatedLinear` under batch invariance; the indexer and compressor projections are unquantized; `lm_head` is vocab-parallel).

## Validation

H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM), torch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, vLLM nightly 0.33.0rc1.dev454 with this diff applied. Tuning: for each shape and `BLOCK_K` in {64, 128}, the fastest (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, num_warps, num_stages) per bucket, timed at the bucket's largest M; the `BLOCK_K` kept has the lowest mean log time ratio to cuBLAS.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py -k hopper_tuned
```

Serving (gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b): fresh `vllm serve` per run, `--max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 32 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 20261105 --num-warmups 20`, 2,000 prompts per run; decode-heavy 512 in / 256 out, prefill-heavy 1,024 in / 4 out; main and patch alternate which goes first, batch invariance off measured in every round.

## Not yet measured

End-to-end runs of GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1 need a full 8-GPU H200/H100 node, which takes days to get on our cluster; in progress. H200 uses the same `hopper` table but was not benchmarked.

Tuning script and raw outputs: https://github.com/imthomp/vllm-batch-invariance (`src/tune_bi.py`, `results/tune`, `results/serve_gptoss`, `results/serve_gptoss120b`).

commits.pr_title: [Config] Make --monokernel and decode_backend=latency_specialized one switch
commits.pr_body:
Human written Summary:

While reviewing this https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66184, which is to use `--monokernal` config to replace the legacy mono-kernel enablement code for MiniMax-M31 ( I did it during Day 0 time which is the early stage of mono-kernel era in vLLM ) using the environment variable, I knew we also have a different way of enabling it. For example, when I enabled the mono kernel for the Mistral-large-4  (PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64534), I used `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}` . so, to make things easier, I put up this PR to let these two config options alias each other .  

## Purpose

Two switches turn on a model's specialized decode (RFC #60904), and each model reads only one:


| Switch | Read by (main) |
| --- | --- |
| `--monokernel` (`KernelConfig.monokernel`) | DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 AMD, Muse Spark AMD, MiniMax-M3 AMD |
| `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'` | DeepSeek-V4.1, GLM5next, Kimi-K3, Muse Spark (NVIDIA); Kimi-K3 AMD; MiniMax-M3.1 NVIDIA (#66324) |
| Both, through a per-model alias | Mistral Large 4 AMD (#64534): its `decode_backend()` returns `latency_specialized` when `kernel_config.monokernel` is set |

Except where a model adds its own alias, as Mistral Large 4 does, the other switch is silently ignored. `additional_config` is not validated, so passing `decode_backend` to an AMD model that reads `--monokernel`, or the reverse, starts the stock decode with no error or log. Recipes that serve one model on both vendors have to pass both switches (Muse Spark already does). MiniMax-M3.1 will have the same split once #66324 (NVIDIA, `decode_backend`) and #66184 (AMD, `--monokernel`) land.

This PR makes them one switch in `VllmConfig.__post_init__`:

- `decode_backend=latency_specialized` sets `kernel_config.monokernel=True`.
- `--monokernel` sets `additional_config["decode_backend"]="latency_specialized"`.
- `--monokernel` with any other `decode_backend` value (e.g. `auto`) is an error.
- Both spellings give the same compile factors, so they share the compile cache.

No model reads both switches with different meanings: each model and vendor directory reads only one, and the CUDA-only hooks in common files are gated on `current_platform.is_cuda()`. The alias therefore only turns on what the user asked for, on the model's own path. A `SupportsCompileFactors` (non-dict) `additional_config` is left unchanged.

Also: the Muse Spark AMD DSpark draft warned "specialized decode is not supported on ROCm" whenever `decode_backend` was set. On AMD that switch now enables the target's monokernel, so the message becomes an info line saying that only the draft keeps its stock layers.

## Not a duplicate

`gh pr list --state open` searches for "monokernel decode_backend", "monokernel alias" and "latency_specialized alias" find model PRs that each use one switch (#61662, #65566, #60889, #65985, #66324, #61568) and a docs PR (#62256) that documents both. None of them unify the two. RFC #60904's text names `decode_backend`, and its comments treat both switches as valid.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/test_config.py -k "monokernel or decode_backend or neither_switch"`: three new tests. Either spelling sets both switches and hashes the same, the default sets neither, and a conflicting `decode_backend` raises.

## Test Result



- With the change: 5 passed. Without it (`vllm/config/vllm.py` reverted): 4 failed, 1 passed (the default case).
- Run against this branch's Python on a ROCm nightly image (`2b009fc`), with the tests in a standalone file. The full `tests/test_config.py` does not collect on that image: its compiled ops are older than main (`torch.ops._C.rotary_embedding` is missing). CI covers the full file.
- Muse Spark ROCm: `import vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.dspark` works; `pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` (CPU tests): 16 passed. The 26 gfx950 tiny-model tests were not run (GPUs busy); they do not cover the changed lines. No Muse Spark serve run (TP8, 816B).
- Muse Spark serve on MI350X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (`153dc0464`, 2026-11-13) with this PR's `vllm/` diff applied, the recipe's AMD MXFP4 command (`amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8 + EP, 7-token DSpark, AITER FA, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), and one chat request ("What is 17 * 23?"):

  | Image | Switch | "Muse Spark monokernel attached" | Draft warning | Answer |
  | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
  | nightly + this PR | `--monokernel` | 8 / 8 ranks | once | `391` |
  | nightly + this PR | `decode_backend=latency_specialized` only | 8 / 8 ranks | once | `391` |
  | nightly (main) | `decode_backend=latency_specialized` only | **0 / 8 ranks** | once | `391` |

  On main, `decode_backend` is silently ignored by the Muse Spark AMD target; with this PR it starts the same monokernel as `--monokernel`. These runs used the earlier warning wording; the final commit changes only the text. The hipBLASLt `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` warnings in the logs (m 8192, n 304-320, k 40960) appear on the unpatched nightly too.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.
- No serving change for existing commands: a deployment that passed one switch keeps the same model path. The only new behavior is that the other spelling now works too.

## Notes

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Select only batch-invariant MXFP8 linear kernels under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the MXFP8 linear kernel selector on CUDA could pick Marlin or FlashInfer, whose output for a row changes with the batch size. This PR gives the MXFP8 linear kernels a `supports_batch_invariance()` capability and, in batch-invariant mode, drops kernels without it before selection. Related: #27433, #65560 (coverage gap "Batch-invariant execution").

## Claims

- With the flag on, MXFP8 linear layers on CUDA only run on kernels that declare batch invariance: Emulation (default), and Humming (`--linear-backend humming`, and still the default on Hopper). A `--linear-backend` that names another kernel falls back to automatic selection with the existing warning.
- This fixes the default configuration on Ampere/Ada (Marlin) and Blackwell (FlashInfer CuTe-DSL), and `--linear-backend marlin` on any GPU.
- No change with the flag off, on ROCm/XPU, or on the MXFP8 BMM path.

## Test

B200 (SM100), main `919d45fc3a` vs this PR `18b921b1ba` (its parent is that main commit), `flashinfer` 0.7.3, `humming-kernels` 0.1.19. Not rerun on H100 or Ampere/Ada for this revision.

```bash
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm serve vllm-project/Qwen3-0.6B-MXFP8 --port 9256 --max-num-seqs 128 --no-enable-prefix-caching

# main
Using FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
Model loading took 0.73 GiB memory and 1.577296 seconds

# now
Using EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
Model loading took 1.14 GiB memory and 1.903502 seconds
```

### Reproduce

```bash
cd tests && VLLM_TEST_MODEL=vllm-project/Qwen3-0.6B-MXFP8 pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN -k TRITON_ATTN

# main
```

commits.pr_title: [Recipe][ROCm] ripple-65b on mi350x and mi355x
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This builds on #66721, which added the AMD section of the Ripple-65B-Preview recipe and marked MI355X verified. On top of it, this PR:

- Marks the BF16 variant verified on MI350X too.
- Adds an AMD override that selects `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, in both the rendered command and the guide's `docker run` example. Without the override, ROCm auto-selects `ROCM_ATTN`, which handles DFlash2 verify steps poorly (in terms of throughput performance): 3x slower on GSM8K and 8.7x slower on SPEED-Bench.
- Caps `--max-model-len` at 1048576 on AMD with or without DFlash2. #66721 capped it only with DFlash2, but the KV cache for the full 2,097,152-token context does not fit on one MI350X with either attention backend.

## Claims

- On 1x MI350X, the recipe's AMD command with DFlash2 (`num_speculative_tokens: 7`) matches published accuracy:
  - GSM8K: 0.9424 (strict).
  - GPQA-Diamond: 83.6 ± 2.3, against 85.2 published. 17 of 792 responses ran out of the 65,536-token context before answering; excluding them gives 85.4.
- Throughput: SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` reaches 470.9 output tok/s at concurrency 16.
- `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` is 3.0x faster than `ROCM_ATTN` on GSM8K and 8.7x faster on SPEED-Bench, with the same accuracy and acceptance length.
- The B300 command does not change.

## Validation

**Setup.** 1x MI350X (gfx950), TP1, BF16.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview` at rev `e27e1717` |
| Drafter | `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2` at rev `35609b3b`, 7 tokens |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly@sha256:6eeac5c6`: vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev142+g96710245e`, AITER `0.1.28.post1`, plus the one-line clamp from ROCm/aiter#7539 |

**Recipe.** `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir recipes` passes at vllm-project/recipes@0eb50b4. On AMD, the recipe resolves to the BF16 variant, because NVFP4 is restricted to Blackwell and Rubin. The renderer emits `--max-model-len 1048576` once on MI350X and MI355X, with and without spec decoding.

**Serve command.** This is the recipe's AMD command with reasoning, tool calling and spec decoding on. The last three flags are not part of the recipe and were added for the benchmarks.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --reasoning-parser ripple \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser ripple \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
```

**Accuracy and throughput:**

| Benchmark | Settings | Result | Wall time | Acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K | lm-eval 0.4.13, 5-shot, 1319 samples, `local-completions`, concurrency 64, `max_gen_toks` 2048 | 0.9424 strict / 0.9416 flexible (± 0.0064) | 188.4 s | 5.81 |
| GPQA-Diamond | temperature 0.7, top_p 0.99, `reasoning_effort` max, 4 epochs, 64 parallel tasks | 83.6 ± 2.3 over 792/792 samples, 0 errors | 1 h 54 min | 4.74 |
| SPEED-Bench | `throughput_8k`, `low_entropy` category, 1024 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, concurrency 16, 256 prompts + 16 warmups | 470.9 output tok/s; median TTFT 1181 ms, median TPOT 32.5 ms | 557 s | 3.31 |

During GPQA, generation throughput averaged 1,060 tok/s at 64 running requests. All 256 SPEED-Bench requests completed, with exactly 1024 output tokens each.

**Attention backends.** After merging main (including #66721), I rebuilt the image from this branch with `docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl` (`vllm-openai` target, gfx950): vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev263+g7b723d043` (same tree as 481ca99fc4, before a sign-off amend), AITER `0.1.29`, plus the ROCm/aiter#7539 clamp. Both runs use the recipe's AMD command as rendered, with DFlash2 (7 tokens) and `--max-model-len 1048576`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. Only `--attention-backend` differs. Benchmark settings match the table above.

| Backend | GSM8K strict / flexible | GSM8K wall time | GSM8K acceptance | SPEED-Bench output tok/s | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | SPEED-Bench acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` | 0.9439 / 0.9431 | 188.5 s | 5.80 | 471.2 | 1182 ms | 32.3 ms | 3.32 |
| `ROCM_ATTN` (auto-selected default) | 0.9416 / 0.9409 | 560.5 s | 5.79 | 54.3 | 15272 ms | 284.4 ms | 3.29 |

Acceptance length is the same for both backends, so the gap is attention time, not drafting. The unified-attention results on the rebuilt image match the nightly results above.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# GSM8K
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048

# GPQA-Diamond
beam-verifier eval gpqa-diamond --base-url http://localhost:8000/v1 \
  --model-name ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview --parallel-tasks 64 --harness-kwargs epochs=4

# SPEED-Bench (data from NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills speed-bench/prepare.py, throughput_8k config)
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview \
  --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path <prepared dir> \
  --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_8k --speed-bench-category low_entropy \
  --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 256 --num-warmups 16 --max-concurrency 16 --seed 0

# Image used for the attention-backend comparison (run from an export of this branch's HEAD)
STACK_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly RUNTIME=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:base-nightly \
  TAG=vllm-rocm:ripple-main docker buildx bake -f docker/docker-bake-rocm.hcl vllm-openai \
  --set vllm-openai.args.ARCH=gfx950
```

</details>

## Details

**Why the override is needed.** `_get_backend_priorities` in `vllm/platforms/rocm.py` lists `ROCM_ATTN` first on gfx950, so it is auto-selected for Ripple. Two parts of its `chunked_prefill_paged_decode` path cost speculative decoding:

- Any query longer than one token goes to the Triton `context_attention_fwd` prefix-prefill kernel. Every DFlash2 verify step is a multi-token query, so each step runs a prefill over the full context.
- The ROCm custom paged-attention kernel is turned off on sliding-window layers, which are 64 of Ripple's 80 layers.

`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` treats spec-decode queries as decode.

#61433 would rank unified attention above `ROCM_ATTN` when spec decoding is on. It is still open, and it would not cover runs without spec decoding.

**Context length.** The guide from #66721 said the full 2,097,152-token context fits without DFlash2. On one MI350X it does not, with either attention backend, so the AMD override now caps `--max-model-len` at 1048576 in both cases. With DFlash2 and unified attention, a needle-retrieval check found the needle at up to 1,022,250 prompt tokens.

Known limitations, not addressed here:

- **GPU memory fault without ROCm/aiter#7539.** With the stock AITER, earlier long GPQA runs with `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` hit `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` after minutes of 64-way spec-decode load. This matches the gfx950 unified-attention block-table prefetch overread that ROCm/aiter#7539 fixes. All runs above use that fix and had no faults. Until it reaches vLLM's AITER pin, long high-concurrency spec-decode runs on gfx950 can still fault.
- **MI355X without DFlash2.** The 1M cap also applies to MI355X, because recipe-level overrides are per brand, not per GPU. MI355X has the same 288 GB of HBM, so it likely hits the same limit, but I did not test it there.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix ROCM_AITER_FA context loss on out-of-order batches
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
A batch can contain a fresh prompt before a request that has cached KV. If the splitter assumes that the first fresh prompt starts the trailing prefill region, it can put the later continuation on a path that ignores its history. The fix changes how the regions are chosen, adds a guard for an all-decode batch whose `max_query_len` is overstated, and sizes the cached-context chunks correctly.
 This PR takes the order-independent split from #63542 (credit @qli88) and adds an all-decode guard for an over-stated `max_query_len`.

## Claims

- Phi-4-mini `niah_single_2` at 30k, 16 concurrent requests: **0.626 → 1.000** on 1× MI300X. Main misses 187 of 500 needles. The earlier three-model run on the same recipe was Phi 0.62 → 1.00, Mistral-7B 0.74 → 1.00, Qwen3-8B 0.99 → 1.00.
- Qwen3-8B, needle planted at token 2048, 64 prompts, concurrency 16: 40k goes from 59/64 to 64/64. 32k stays 64/64 on both arms.
- Short context is unaffected. Qwen3-8B on the same GPU stays within 0.2% at 8k/1k (concurrency 8 and 32) and at 32k/1k. Total tok/s, TTFT, and TPOT all hold.
- The Phi 30k bench is slower on this PR (29,911 → 28,034 tok/s, TTFT 7.27 s → 8.00 s) because main skips the KV. On that bench main leaves 233,430 context tokens unread (28.9% of the KV, 17.1% of prefill attention). This PR reads all 808,402. 574,972 + 233,430 = 808,402.
- The real-backend unordered-batch test fails on `main` and passes here. The all-decode guard is the case #63542 still fails.

## Validation

Image for every run below: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-96710245ece8fe57a0df3ea18cdc79cbb8ce93cf`
(vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev142+g96710245e`). Both arms are that image; the PR arm only bind-mounts
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` and `rocm_aiter_fa.py`. Every log contains
`Using ROCM_AITER_FA backend (selected via --attention-backend)`.

---

## Performance

### 1. Short context — unchanged

A prompt that fits in one chunk never produces the mixed batch this PR fixes, so nothing should
move. Qwen3-8B, same GPU, main then PR:

```bash
# 1x MI300X
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 40960 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching

vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 --request-rate inf \
  --ignore-eos --seed 2 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot --metric-percentiles 50,99
```

The other rows use the same command with `(8192, 1024, 64, 32)` and `(32768, 1024, 16, 8)`.

| ISL / OSL / conc | prompts | total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k / 8 | 32 | 6087 → 6094 (+0.1%) | 1.41 → 1.47 s | 10.45 → 10.38 ms |
| 8k / 1k / 32 | 64 | 9966 → 9988 (+0.2%) | 3.10 → 3.09 s | 25.81 → 25.76 ms |
| 32k / 1k / 8 | 16 | 8232 → 8231 (−0.0%) | 6.64 → 6.78 s | 25.54 → 25.40 ms |

Phi-4-mini at 8k behaves the same way (output length 128, concurrency 16, 32 prompts):

| prompt / conc | total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8192 / 16 | 34525 → 36201 | 1.38 → 1.25 s | 19.3 → 18.9 ms |

### 2. Long context — Proof that the fix works

Same Phi-4-mini server, prompts long enough that a continuation chunk shares a batch with a fresh
prompt:

| prompt / conc | prompts | total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 30000 / 16 | 16 | 29911 → 28034 (−6.3%) | 7.27 → 8.00 s | 67.1 → 70.0 ms |

Main is faster here because it is doing less work: the rows it misclassifies are attended with
`cu_seqlens_k = query_start_loc`, so `seq − query` tokens of history are never read. The same bench
was rerun with a counter on the prefill slice (`logs/ctx_main.log`, `logs/ctx_pr.log`). Ten chunks
on main were in that state, each a 30k request:

```
q=5424/seq=30000/drop=24576      q=5271/seq=30000/drop=24729      q=5250/seq=30000/drop=24750
q=8088/seq=30000/drop=21912      q=7977/seq=30000/drop=22023      q=7998/seq=30000/drop=22002
q=5331/seq=30000/drop=24669      q=5244/seq=30000/drop=24756
q=8016/seq=30000/drop=21984      q=7971/seq=30000/drop=22029
```

| | context tokens read | context tokens skipped | attention work skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | 574,972 | 233,430 (28.9%) | 17.1% |
| this PR | 808,402 | 0 | 0 |

574,972 + 233,430 = 808,402: the PR reads exactly the tokens main skips. Main drops 28.9% of the
context, which is 17.1% of the prefill attention work; the MLP still runs on every token, which is
why 17% less attention becomes a 6% throughput gap and a 10% TTFT gap rather than something larger.

The regression is the cost of being correct — the skipped tokens are the dropped history that the
accuracy numbers below measure.

---

## Accuracy

### 1. Short context — unchanged, both correct

Qwen3-8B, needle planted at token 2048 so it sits inside the first 8192-token chunk. 64 prompts,
concurrency 16, greedy. At 32,768 the prompt length is an exact multiple of the chunk budget, so a
fresh prefill and a continuation never share a batch:

| prompt | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32768 | 64/64 | 64/64 |

### 2. Long context — main loses the needle, the PR does not
`lm_eval niah_single_2` at 30,000 tokens, 500 samples, prompt length 29,990–29,998:

```bash
# 1x MI300X
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks niah_single_2 --batch_size 1 --seed 4321 \
  --model_args model=microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[30000],"tokenizer":"microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct"}' \
  --log_samples --output_path out/
```

| | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| niah_single_2 @ 30k | 0.626 ± 0.022 | 1.000 |

Same recipe across three models, `num_concurrent=16`; each cell logged
`Using ROCM_AITER_FA backend` before the score was counted:

| Model | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Phi-4-mini-instruct | 0.62 | 1.00 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 0.74 | 1.00 |
| Qwen3-8B | 0.99 | 1.00 |

Qwen3-8B barely moves; Phi-4-mini and Mistral are the models that expose the bug. The Phi row with
the stderr above is the rerun of that first cell.


### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py::test_rocm_aiter_fa_unordered_batch -v
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py -v
```

| test | main | #63542 alone | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test_rocm_aiter_fa_unordered_batch` (2 cases) | 2 failed | — | 2 passed |
| `..._extends[fresh_prompt_sorts_before_extend]` | FAIL | pass | pass |
| `..._extends[all_decode_with_draft_tokens]` | FAIL | FAIL | pass |
| `test_split_dcp_context_queries_counts_a_stale_max_query_len_batch` | FAIL | FAIL | pass |

`split_decodes_prefills_and_extends` has two callers: `rocm_aiter_fa.py` and `cp_utils.py` (NVIDIA DCP). The last row is that second caller. On 8× H200, Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP4, DCP2, FA3, the stock splitter misplaced rows on 24 of 248 calls and this PR on 0. Output under FA3 was 16/16 identical, so that path shows no output change here.

## Details

A batch can contain a fresh prompt before a request that has cached KV. If the splitter assumes
that the first fresh prompt starts the trailing prefill region, it can put the later continuation
on a path that ignores its history. This PR changes how the regions are chosen, sizes the
cached-context chunks correctly, and guards one edge case in the decode count.

### Fix 1 — Find the Last Request with Context

The main cause of the lost-context bug is that MRV2 can place a fresh Prefill request before an
Extend request, while the attention splitter assumes all Extend requests come before Prefill
requests.

As a result, the splitter treats every request after that Prefill as a Prefill too, so the Extend
requests among them are attended without their cached KV history.

To fix this, we find the **last request with cached context** and place the Prefill boundary
immediately after it. Any fresh Prefill requests before this boundary are handled by the Extend
path, which can safely process requests with zero cached context.


### Fix 2 — share the cached-context budget correctly

Because Fix A can place context-free rows in the extend region, the workspace divisor must count
only the rows that actually read context:

```python
num_extends_with_context = max(int((computed_kv_lens > 0).sum()), 1)
max_context_chunk = _CP_TOKENS_PER_ITER_ROCM // num_extends_with_context
```

Dividing by `num_extends` reserves workspace for rows that read nothing, which shrinks everyone
else's chunk and raises `num_chunks = cdiv(max_context, max_context_chunk)`. This is a chunking
change only — it does not alter which rows read their context.

### Fix 3 — Handle All-Decode Batches

There is another edge case where all requests in the attention batch are Decode-like, but
`max_query_len` is larger than the actual query lengths, which can happen during adaptive
speculative verification.

In this case, the original code skips the all-Decode fast path and tries to find the first
non-Decode request. Since no such request exists, `argmax()` returns `0`, incorrectly reporting
zero Decode requests.

**Fix:** We check whether all requests are Decode-like and directly return:

```python
return num_reqs, 0, 0, num_tokens, 0, 0
```

Where:
- `num_reqs`: every request in the batch, all of them Decodes.
- `num_tokens`: every token in the batch, all of them Decode tokens.
- The remaining zeros indicate that there are no Extend or Prefill requests or tokens.

This avoids searching for a non-existent boundary and ensures the entire batch is correctly
processed as Decode.

- [x] **Design Fit:** One splitter shared with #63542, plus the all-decode guard that rewrite does not have.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Reproducer fails on main and passes here. Throughput reported as total tok/s, TTFT, and TPOT.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Comments kept to what the code cannot say.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Dump child process stacks when an AMD CI test times out
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

AMD CI jobs (e.g. V1 Metrics in [build 102446](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102446)) sometimes hang while an EngineCore starts and end with `Timeout (0:25:00)!`, but the dump only shows the pytest process. This makes the `amd_ci_fast_exit` plugin also dump the stacks and kernel wait channels of every child process when a test outlives `faulthandler_timeout`.

## Claims

- When an AMD CI test runs past `faulthandler_timeout` (1500 s), the log now shows each descendant process (including `VLLM::EngineCore` grandchildren): pid/ppid/state/cmdline, per-thread kernel wait channels, and a `py-spy dump --native` stack (gdb fallback).
- Best-effort and bounded (16 processes, 60 s per tool call, 10 min total, 64 KiB per process). It never changes a test result.
- Only affects AMD CI: the plugin is loaded only via `-p amd_ci_fast_exit` in `run-amd-test.sh`. No new dependency (`py-spy==0.4.1` is already in `requirements/test/rocm.txt`, `psutil` in `common.txt`).

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fails before (origin/main plugin + new test) | `pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py -k child` | 3/3 failed |
| Passes after, py-spy 0.4.1 on PATH | same | 5/5 passed (`hang_in_child` / `hang_in_grandchild` frames asserted) |
| Passes after, no py-spy or gdb | same | 1/1 passed (wait-channel output still present) |
| Full test file | `pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` | 13/13 passed |
| Real engine on MI355X (1 GPU) | `LLM(distilgpt2)` test with `-p amd_ci_fast_exit -o faulthandler_timeout=12` | `stacks of 1 child processes`, `VLLM::EngineCore` header, wait channels `futex_wait_queue_me x28, ep_poll x8, ..., kfd_wait_on_events x1`, py-spy stack in `gpu_worker.init_device`; test still passed (exit 0) |
| Lint | `uvx pre-commit run --files <both files>` | all hooks pass |

Manual check of the output: `py-spy --native` showed `clock_nanosleep (libc.so.6)` under `hang_in_child` and `hang_in_grandchild` for both processes.

## Details

**Root cause of the useless dump.** The `Timeout (0:25:00)!` banner is pytest's faulthandler plugin: `run-amd-test.sh` sets `-o faulthandler_timeout=1500` in `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`. It does not kill the job; pytest-timeout (`PYTEST_TIMEOUT=2400`, thread method) does so 15 minutes later. In log 102446 the engine started at 10:14, faulthandler fired at 25 min and pytest-timeout ended the job at about 10:54. Both dumps show only the pytest process, sitting in zmq poll inside `wait_for_engine_startup`. The EngineCore child that actually hangs is never shown, so these 14 hangs in 72 h (all passing on retry) cannot be diagnosed.

**Fix.** A `pytest_runtest_protocol` hookwrapper in `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fast_exit.py` starts a daemon `threading.Timer` at `faulthandler_timeout + 1` s (covering setup, call and teardown, like faulthandler; the extra second avoids interleaving with faulthandler's output) and cancels it when the test ends. On fire, it walks `psutil.Process().children(recursive=True)` and for each process writes a header (pid, ppid, state, cmdline), a count of `/proc/<pid>/task/*/wchan` values (no ptrace needed; shows waits like `kfd_wait_on_events` or futex), then `py-spy dump --native --pid`, falling back to `gdb -batch -ex 'thread apply all bt'`, else one line saying why the stack dump failed. Everything is in a try/except and writes to the stderr fd saved before pytest captures output. The 10 min budget ends well before the pytest-timeout kill.

New test `tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py`: a test whose child spawns a grandchild and both hang, run with `faulthandler_timeout=1`, asserting both processes get a header and wait-channel line, the dump ends with its closing marker, and (if py-spy or gdb is installed) the `hang_in_child` / `hang_in_grandchild` frames appear.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- py-spy/gdb need ptrace permission on a non-ancestor process. The container here has `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` (`ptrace_scope=1`). If CI pods drop it, the dump prints `stack dump failed: py-spy: exit ...` plus wait channels and cmdline, which still narrows things down but has no stacks.
- py-spy only shows threads with Python frames (native frames merged in). Pure-native HIP/ROCr threads (e.g. rocprofiler queue-intercept threads, the suspected trigger) are visible only through wait-channel counts. Adding gdb to the test-deps stage of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` would show every native thread; the plugin already uses gdb when py-spy fails. Not added here.
- The dump also fires for tests that are only slow (over 25 min) and then pass. `py-spy dump` briefly pauses each target while reading it; this only adds output and does not change the result.

**Duplicate-work check.** Searched open PRs for `py-spy rocm ci`, `amd_ci_fast_exit`, `faulthandler_timeout`, `stack dump child process timeout ci` and `engine startup hang stack dump`; none covers this. #49628 (opt-in diagnostics for stalled engine stages) is an engine-side feature, not CI tooling. #64752 (skip kineto promotion when `HSA_TOOLS_LIB` is set) is related to the suspected trigger of these hangs but is not a diagnostics change. #67567 also edits `tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` (signal-state independence); the two changes do not overlap and apply cleanly in either order.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Re-enable VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error in the ROCm test image
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Turns `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` back on in the ROCm test image, so AMD CI flags GPU<->CPU syncs in `execute_model`/`sample_tokens` the same way CUDA CI does (`docker/Dockerfile` sets the same ENV). #61939 dropped the ENV from `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`.

**Depends on #66397, #66400, #66398, #66399. Merge this one last.** Those PRs fix the syncs that failed 16 AMD groups at 8 sites when the check was on ([vllm/ci #97758](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758), [vllm/amd-ci #15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532)). If this lands first, those groups go red again.

This PR reuses #64176. Its first version wrapped all 8 sites in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. `njhill` pointed out that most or all of them could be fixed, so the fixes now live in the four PRs above. This PR keeps only the ENV and the test-instrumentation allow.

## Claims

- `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`: `ENV VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` goes in the per-commit `test` stage, below the `==== per-commit stages: nothing below is part of the runtime key ====` marker. The content-keyed `runtime`/`test-deps` images keep their keys and are not rebuilt.
- `tests/models/test_dsv4{,1}_mono_layers.py`: the `MonoProbe` forward hooks copy decoder-layer outputs and routing margins to the host from inside `execute_model` (`.tolist()`, `.cpu()`). They are test instrumentation, not engine code, so they now run under `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This follows `test_mm_prefix_lm.py` and `test_hisparse.py`. No engine code changes.
  - How these syncs were found: a `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` run of `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -k 2-8` (TP2, gfx950) with #66397's fix reported only the hook lines (`keep`: `pos.tolist()`, `t[row].float().cpu()`; `gap_hook`: `.tolist()`), apart from the indexer `dcp_rank_tensor` site that #66397 removes.
  - Why allow instead of deferring `.cpu()` to `save_capture()`: the hooks dedupe captures by host position (`setdefault` on `(layer, prompt len, position)`) and read the reused `positions` buffer. Deferring would mean cloning every layer's `(x, residual)` and positions on device every decode step and resolving keys after the run. That is a larger rewrite of test-only code, for no engine benefit.

## Validation

Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13, amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1.

| Check (this branch) | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` (Dockerfile/build structure) | 46 passed |
| `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py --collect-only` | 6 collected |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed |

**Integration run on the final stack:** `main` (`5629b26146`) + all commits of #66397, #66400, #66398, #66399, then this PR's two commits, cherry-picked in that order. Each row ran from `tests/` with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. `syncs` = `grep -c "sync detected"` on the log.

The checker is armed only after warmup, inside a worker's `execute_model`/`sample_tokens`. **Armed** rows go through that path, so `0` there is evidence of no syncs. **Not armed** rows call kernels or backends in-process without arming the checker. They are correctness checks only, and their `0` says nothing about syncs.

| Group | Checker | Result | syncs |
|---|---|---|---|

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model] Run Qwen3.5 on the eager breakable-graph model on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a ROCm variant of the eager Qwen3.5 model (`vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/`), uses it with breakable CUDA graphs by default on ROCm, and adds an MI355 mirror for the B200 `Qwen3.5` step.

## Claims

- `qwen3_5/amd/model.py`, `amd/mtp.py`: copy of the NVIDIA model with the ROCm counterparts of its fusions: Triton Gemma RMSNorm, the row-parallel all-reduce deferred into AITER's fused all-reduce + Gemma RMSNorm (when AITER custom all-reduce is on), the strided-z GDN gated norm, and the fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate kernel. Keeps AITER fused shared-expert weight rerouting like the legacy ROCm model.
- `qwen3_5/__init__.py`, `config/vllm.py`: ROCm picks the AMD model and adds the Qwen3.5 archs to the ROCm breakable-graph default, on every arch. None of the kernels the AMD model adds needs a specific arch: the Gemma norm, the fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate and the strided-z gated norm are plain Triton, and the AITER fused all-reduce + norm runs only when AITER custom all-reduce is on, with a plain all-reduce + norm fallback.
- `fused_gdn_gated_norm.py` moves from `qwen3_5/nvidia/ops/` to `qwen3_5/common/`, unchanged, since both models use it.
- `qwen3_next.py`: splits the platform-independent `supports_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate` out of `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate`. The value of `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate` does not change for any model.
- Tests: new `test_amd_model.py` (Qwen3.5-0.8B vs HF greedy logprobs, TP1 Triton path and TP2 AITER path), dispatch and breakable-default cases in `test_qwen3_5.py` and `test_config.py`, the gated-norm tests in `test_gdn_output_projection.py` now also run on ROCm (FP8 output on gfx950), and `test_fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py` asserts that the AITER fused all-reduce path is the one taken on ROCm.
- `models_basic.yaml`: `mirror.amd` on `mi355_2` that runs `models/qwen3_5/` plus `kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py`.
- `spec_decode.yaml`: the MI355 `Spec Decode MTP Qwen3.5` mirror now also triggers on `vllm/models/qwen3_5/` and `qwen3_next.py`, so changes to `amd/mtp.py` run the MTP e2e tests.

## Validation

All runs on MI355X (gfx950). A reviewer checked gfx942 (model test on both paths, two-module MTP, latency at parity with the compiled model). gfx90a, RDNA and gfx1250 were not run; they take the same path by code reading.

Mirror command, from `tests/`, 2 GPUs, default ROCm CI env:

```bash
pytest -v -s models/qwen3_5/ kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py
```

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| 10 back-to-back runs after rebasing on current main | 10/10 passed, each 20 passed and 50 skipped (129-145 s) |
| 10 back-to-back runs after unifying the ROCm gating | 10/10 passed, each 20 passed and 82 skipped (116-133 s) |

The passes are `test_amd_model` x2, the strided-z gated norm x8, its FP8 output x9 and the output projection x1. The 82 skips are the NVIDIA-only tests in `models/qwen3_5/` (SM100 FP8/NVFP4 norm-quant, FlashInfer all-reduce + norm-quant, CUDA aux-stream `in_proj_ba` overlap). The AMD model does not use those paths. The skip count is 82 instead of 50 because main has since added more NVIDIA-only tests under `models/qwen3_5/`. `test_fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py` already runs on MI355 in the MiniMax Reduce RMS mirror, so it is not repeated here. With the new assertion it passes on 2 GPUs (12 passed, 6 world_size=4 skipped), and it fails when AITER is off, as expected.

Nearby suites on the final diff: `test_qwen3_5.py` + `test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py` 22 passed, `test_config.py -k "qwen3_5 or breakable or rocm"` 45 passed, `test_initialization.py -k Qwen3_5` 7 passed (6 of them on the AMD model, incl. MoE and MTP; `ColQwen3_5` still imports the old `model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py`). Before the rebase, `generation_ppl_test` Qwen3.5 also passed. On CPU torch, the new cases in `test_qwen3_5.py` and `test_breakable_cudagraph_platform_default` pass (17 passed); their teardown errors come from the shared `cleanup_fixture`, which needs an accelerator and is unchanged from main. The 11 failures in the full files fail the same way on main.

A mutation check: switching the AMD GDN gated norm from silu to sigmoid makes `test_amd_model` fail.

gsm8k (`tests/evals/gsm8k`), main vs this PR:

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| CI `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DEP2` (0.84 +- 0.03) | 0.8613, 0.8658, 0.8681, 0.8666 | 10/10 pass: 0.848-0.864, mean 0.859 |
| CI `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8-DEP2` (0.79 +- 0.03) | 5 runs: 0.7794-0.7930, mean 0.788 +- 0.007 | 5 runs: 0.8143-0.8340, mean 0.824 +- 0.007 |
| CI `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4-AITER-TP2` (0.89 +- 0.03) | 0.8916 | 0.8916 |
| CI `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4-EMU-TP2` (0.89 +- 0.03) | 0.8969 | 0.8878 |
| Qwen3.5-4B TP1, 5-shot chat greedy | 0.8969 | 0.8939 |
| Qwen3.5-4B TP2 (AITER) | 0.8901 | 0.8946 |

Run to run, the same config moves by about 1-2 points. The FP8 config is the exception: over 5 interleaved runs per side, this PR scores 3.7 points higher than main and the ranges do not overlap, but neither path is more accurate. Almost every answer starts with an empty-or-real `<think>` choice whose two candidate tokens are often an exact bf16 logit tie, and greedy breaks ties toward the long reasoning path, which overruns `max_tokens`. Main lands on that tie slightly more often (12.7% vs 10.8% of questions). With the lm_head in fp32 both paths score about 0.87 (main 0.869/0.874, PR 0.886/0.874). Details and the eval fix: #66985. The other rows stay within noise. `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-DEP2` was not run.

Perf, Qwen3.5-4B, `vllm bench latency` with input 512, decode/step = (latency at 65 output tokens - at 1) / 64, median of 3 interleaved rounds:

| TP | BS | AITER | prefill main ms | prefill PR ms | decode main ms | decode PR ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | off | 20.8 | 14.3 | 2.916 | 2.888 (-1.0%) |
| 1 | 32 | off | 180.9 | 175.7 | 4.750 | 4.611 (-2.9%) |
| 2 | 1 | on | 18.7 | 14.4 | 2.533 | 2.496 (-1.5%) |
| 2 | 32 | on | 202.0 | 204.3 | 4.108 | 4.157 (+1.2%) |

`vllm bench throughput` (Qwen3.5-4B TP1, random 1024/256, 512 prompts, 3 interleaved rounds): 42360/42517/42461 -> 42931/43022/43082 tok/s.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files. `check_test_tethering.py --all` reports only the same allowlist note it reports on main.

## Details

On gfx950 the NVIDIA eager model with only a Triton norm was slower than the compiled model, because the q/k Gemma norms and mrope ran unfused in eager mode (about 107 more elementwise kernels per step). With the fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate kernel turned on in the AMD model, it is at parity or a little faster, as the tables show. The one slower cell, TP2 bs32 with AITER (+1.2%), uses AITER's GDN path, which does not call the fused gated norm.

Left out for now. The FP8/NVFP4 norm + input-quant fusions: no ROCm Qwen3.5 checkpoint uses static per-tensor FP8 input scales, and the ROCm-relevant per-token FP8 and MXFP4/MXFP8 variants need their own kernels and evals. The `in_proj_ba` aux-stream overlap stays CUDA-only, because enabling it on ROCm hung in breakable piecewise capture. The model copy follows the `minimax_m3/amd` pattern so the NVIDIA model stays untouched.

This does not duplicate an open PR. Searches for Qwen3.5 with ROCm, AMD, gfx950, MI355 and breakable found no PR that adds a ROCm Qwen3.5 model package. Related PRs that will conflict textually: #51406 enables the fused QK-norm/RoPE/gate kernel in the compiled ROCm path through the same `qwen3_next.py` lines. #66160 edits `fused_gdn_gated_norm.py`, which this PR moves to `common/`. #64687 makes the same kind of port for XPU in `qwen3_5/__init__.py`, `config/vllm.py` and `test_qwen3_5.py`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Make /ci rocm cache a cache-only CI build that also copies the runtime
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`/ci rocm cache` now runs as a CI build that only copies images, and it copies the PR's runtime and test-deps images along with the stack, so `main` stops rebuilding them after the merge. Rebased onto current `main`; supersedes this PR's earlier version.

## Claims

- The cache build is a `main` build of the ci pipeline that runs only the new `rocm-base-image-cache` step (`VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS`), instead of an AMD CI build. No ci-infra change is needed; ci-infra's AMD CI promote mode (ci-infra#886) can be removed after this merges.
- `build.sh promote` copies the PR's runtime and test-deps images too, so `main` reuses them when it has the same runtime key after the merge. After #65937, `main`'s first build spent 31 min in "Ensure ROCm stack + runtime" (ci build 100464) rebuilding a runtime and test-deps that the PR's CI had already built under those keys.
- Only images the PR's CI build pushed on top of a parent it also pushed are recorded and copied, so a retried job or another PR overwriting this PR's tags can't pair the copied stack with a runtime built on a different one.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` | 53 passed; the new recording, copy-chain and no-request tests fail on `main`'s `build.sh` |
| `cd .github/workflows/scripts && pytest test_run_ci_command.py` | 74 passed, 117 subtests |
| ci-infra's `pipeline_generator` run on this branch, `main` build with `VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS=["rocm-base-image-cache"]` | exactly one step, queue `amd-cpu`, `ROCM_CI_REPO: rocm/vllm-ci`, no image builds |
| same, nightly (`NIGHTLY=1`) | step included; `promote` exits 0 without `ROCM_PROMOTE_PR` |
| same, normal `main` build | step only offered under "Run more jobs" |
| `pre-commit` on the changed files | clean |

Not run end to end: an actual cache build on the ci pipeline (it needs a PR that changes the ROCm stack and a maintainer's `/ci rocm cache`).

## Details

- `build.sh` base mode records `rocm-rocm-{runtime,test-deps}-built` like `rocm-rocm-stack-built`, but only when the same job also pushed the parent (a `BUILT_HERE` file, since each `ensure` runs in a subshell); building a stack resets both to `none`, because metadata outlives a retried job. `promote` copies stack-wheels, stack, runtime, test-deps in order, each child only over a parent this run copied, never over an image `main` built; a missing child record stops the chain with exit 0.
- The step lives in `.buildkite/image_build/amd_rocm_cache.yaml`. ci-infra's AMD CI pipeline renders every file in `hardware_tests/`, but only the main pipeline lists `image_build/`. It is optional. Nightlies still run optional steps, so without a request `promote` exits 0 right after its arguments, before the builder, build context or tag fetch. It also validates the PR number and commit format that ci-infra's `bootstrap-amd.sh` used to check.
- The handler still looks for the source build in both pipelines, since PRs still run AMD CI (#66596's cache came from an AMD CI build).
- Limits: if `main` changes a runtime-key input (requirements, `Dockerfile.rocm` above the marker) between the PR's CI build and the merge, the copied runtime is unused and `main` rebuilds it as before (#66596: 46 min). A retried promote finishes the chain: an existing tag holding the digest the PR's CI recorded is an earlier attempt's copy, and only a different digest is treated as `main`'s.

## Overview DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash does not run on A100 today: its attention, indexer and cache codecs need FlashMLA, DeepGEMM and FP8/FP4 conversion instructions that SM80 lacks; on H100, `main` runs it on its stock kernels. This PR serves the model on one 8×A100 or 8×H100 node with decode kernels written in CuTe DSL, all under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`; other GPUs keep their current path. Accuracy is on par with `main` on GB300, and in AgentX H100 reaches 1.5–1.7× the P90 interactivity of InferenceX's H100 vLLM line. ![DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash AgentX on 8×H100 and 8×A100, this PR against InferenceX's H100 vLLM line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaoyaoding/vllm/19f66703fce5da5fc12b706a6525d3adb2040fcc/sm80_sm90_agentx.png) ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves on 8×A100 (SM80) at TP8, with DSpark speculative decoding. - On 8×H100 (SM90), the decode path reaches 489 P90 tok/s per user at one request in AgentX, against 324 for InferenceX's H100 vLLM line. - Accuracy on both matches `main` on GB300 (GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, AIME25, RULER NIAH up to 256K). ## Validation ### Accuracy Stock vLLM does not run DeepSeek-V4.1 on A100, so the reference is `main` on one GB300 tray as measured for #63921 (same checkpoint, tasks and sampling). The A100 column was measured on an earlier revision of this PR, on `main` `8530a778`, and the H100 column on its head `a68e7c37` with the default MoE path (Humming W4A8); both at TP8 with DSpark verifying for real. the fused Markov loop .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/ampere \ tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/hopper/test_indexer_metadata.py \ tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_quantization.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_mhc_dispatch.py \ tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_fused_markov.py -v # 8x H100: the SM90 attention, indexer and fused all-reduce;
